> **Generated — do not hand-edit this table.** Each row's source is
> `_registry/<CR###>.row.md` (one file per CR); rebuild with
> `scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. See [How a CR works](#how-a-cr-works).

The register of **planned change** — new work, not fixes. A CR is anything that adds or
changes behaviour versus the current build: a feature, a refactor, a process change, a
content or infra change. (Fixing something already broken is a **Defect** —
see [`../defect/def_list.md`](../defect/def_list.md).)

Governance rationale: decision **D-058** in [`../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md`](../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md).

## How a CR works

- **This table is generated — never hand-edit it.** Each row's source is
  `_registry/CR###.row.md` (one file per CR = a disjoint write-path); rebuild with
  `python scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen cr`. A shared monolithic table gets *swept*
  on the shared `main` checkout ([CR081](CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only.md));
  one-file-per-item removes the shared write entirely.
- **Auto-file, proceed.** Saiful's prompt IS the approval. When he asks for a change, the
  **Architect mints the next `CR###`** (one minter, no ID-collision race); its **domain
  owner** writes `_registry/CR###.row.md` + creates the folder + files the CR doc, then
  implements — no separate approval gate. A web CR's row is written by `coder.web`, a backend
  CR's by `coder.api`, etc. — the register is no longer an Architect chokepoint (it only mints
  the number, which is domain-agnostic).
- **ID:** `CR###`, zero-padded, sequential, never reused.
- **Folder:** every CR gets `docs/forward_planning/CR###_<snake_case_topic>/`. It holds at
  minimum `CR###_<topic>.md` (what / why / scope / acceptance). All design docs, notes, and
  sub-specs for that change live in its folder.
- **Regenerate + pathspec-commit:** after writing/editing a row file, run the generator and
  `git commit -m "…" -- <your row file> docs/forward_planning/cr_list.md`. Never bare /
  `-am` / `git add -A`.
- **Commit tag:** the fix/feat commit carries `(AT:R<N> CR###)` after the summary, e.g.
  `feat(journal): search across entries (AT:R42 CR007)`.
- **Exempt from needing a CR:** process commits — handover wraps (`chore(handover)`),
  TestFlight/build version bumps, and docs-only commits. These keep the plain `(AT:R<N>)` tag.

**Status:** one of exactly five tokens — `proposed` · `in_progress` · `done` · `dropped` ·
`standing` (an ongoing order with no completion date, e.g. CR060's content-quality
mandate) — and nothing else. Qualifiers go in the description column.

**Enforced** (DEF203) by `gen_registers.py verify` and
`backend/tests/unit/test_registers_no_drift.py`. The vocabulary deliberately differs from
the defect register's: a CR is planned work that can sit in progress, a defect is broken or
it is not. This line previously omitted `standing` and the register carried `started`,
`partial` and `in progress` alongside `in_progress`.

| CR077 | 2026-07-23 | **Prompt caching is already on, delivers 0% on Room prompts, and could not have helped much anyway.** Saiful: *"lots of our messages to the llm are static, especially for the agents. is there a way we can speed up the processing by pre-caching a major part of the prompt?"* The premise is right; the conclusion doesn't follow. **Measured on the live serving host** (`192.168.20.74:8000`, vLLM `0.23.1.dev0`, `ami-llm` = `RedHatAI/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4`): prefix caching is **already enabled** (`enable_prefix_caching="True"`, lifetime 17,151,568/50,924,616 = 33.7% of queried tokens) — nothing to turn on. But `ami-llm` is a **Mamba/attention hybrid**, so vLLM auto-resolves `block_size` up to **2,096 tokens** to align the Mamba and attention pages, and caching is whole-block only. **Measured cliff: a 2,095-token prompt repeated verbatim reuses 0 tokens; 2,096 reuses a full block** — and every reuse observed was a multiple of 2,096 (2096/4192/6288/14672). Every Room agent system prompt is **1,143–2,264 tokens** (the static base+overlay part only 635–1,387), so the Room gets **exactly zero** cache benefit today; the 33.7% comes from elsewhere. Known upstream issue, not our misconfiguration — vllm-project/vllm #40696. The twelve agents also share **no** common prefix: `build_agent_prompt()` puts `content/agents/<id>.md` at token 0, so they diverge on the first token. **And fixing it wouldn't matter: prefill is ~4% of a turn.** Decode measured at **33.0 tok/s** single-stream (200 tok in 6.07 s, 400 in 11.89 s — same rate); prefilling a whole 1,300-token prompt costs **0.29 s** against **~7.6 s** to generate a 250-token turn. Perfect caching of 100% of every prompt cuts a convene ~4%. **The real lever is concurrency.** Same host, `min_tokens` forced, streams salted against cache cross-talk: 1→33.0 tok/s, 2→57.1 (1.73×), 4→91.1 (**2.77×**), 8→150.5 (**4.57×**) aggregate; and the card is at `gpu_memory_utilization=0.5` with 3.49M tokens of KV cache — half unused. `room_runner.py:1375-1393` runs all twelve agents strictly sequentially. Exactly one phase could change: **ANALYSTS** (fundamentals/market/news/social, four independent domains) — ~4×6.1 s becomes ~8.8 s, **~15 s off a convene, ~4× what perfect caching could ever deliver**. RESEARCHERS (bear answers bull) and RISK (three debators) must stay sequential — the dependency is the point. **The catch, raised by this lane not discovered later:** every prompt carries `Transcript so far:` and *"build on the transcript — do not repeat what's already been said"* (`room_prompts.py:214,220`), so concurrent analysts go blind to each other and will repeat. That is a **Room-quality** call, decided by reading real output, not by reasoning — hence **Phase 1 is a blocking A/B on 5 tickers, and no code ships before it**; if quality drops the CR closes at a documented "no". Phase 2 parallelises ANALYSTS only, behind a `parallel: bool` on `_Phase` with deterministic `RoomEvent` ordering; Phase 3 raises `gpu_memory_utilization` (ops on the LLM host — this workstation has no SSH to it). **Explicitly refused:** restructuring prompts to build a ≥2,096-token shared prefix. It moves the per-agent persona to the *end*, colliding with the safety-floor ordering rule (`agent_prompts.py:64-65` — the floor is appended last *so it dominates*) and CR038's ~70% instruction-compliance finding. Room-quality risk of that size for 4% of wall clock is a bad trade; revisit only if upstream lands sub-block caching. **Silent-failure trap recorded** for whoever does: in `align` cache mode (ours), if the Mamba checkpoint lands in request-unique tokens vLLM discards the *entire* prefix match including perfectly-matched attention blocks, and the hit rate drops to zero with no signal — vllm-project/vllm #45238. CR040's degrade-loudly class arriving from inside the inference server; hence the second guard, **log the measured hit rate at startup** — nobody would currently notice if caching were off. First guard: a test asserting the phases marked parallel are exactly the phases whose agents don't read each other — someone later marking RISK parallel would silently delete the risk debate while every test passes and the UI still renders three contributions, which is DEF084's shape. Also flagged in passing: CLAUDE.md's runtime table still says the LLM is *"Gemma 4 31B"*; the host reports **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4**. Brief — architect/build team implements; this lane files and reviews.  **AMENDED same day — Saiful: *"concierge take 20K token"*, and that flips the answer for one surface.** The Concierge system prompt measures **15,731 tokens**, of which **14,558 is the lesson catalogue** — `_full_context_index()` rendering all **342** lessons (`concierge_prompts.py:317`, CR020 `full_context`), **byte-identical for every user** and changing only when a lesson is added. That is 7 whole cache blocks of exactly the static text Saiful described — and it caches **nothing**, because `build_concierge_messages()` (`:103-131`) puts it **behind** ~900 tokens of per-user text (mandate overlay, mandate one-liner, journal, unlocked agents). A prefix cache matches from token 0 and stops at the first difference, so one differing mandate field invalidates all 14,558 tokens behind it; the cacheable prefix is `base` alone at **892 tokens — under the 2,096 cliff, so zero**. **Measured A/B against the live cache, two users differing only in mandate:** current order → 2nd user gets **0 cached, 2,672 ms**; catalogue-first → 2nd user gets **14,672 cached, 344 ms**. **7.8×, 2.33 s saved per message**, for the cost of moving one block earlier in an f-string. **Not oversold:** within one conversation the system prompt is already identical turn-to-turn, so today's shape already caches from turn 2 (measured same-user: 2,674 → 389 → 391 ms). The reorder buys **the first message of every conversation for every user after the first** — the message users actually notice. **Second-order win, arguably bigger:** today each user needs a private 15.7K-token KV copy (~222 concurrent contexts fit in the 3.49M-token cache, evicting Room traffic when they don't); shared-prefix, all users draw on **one** copy and need ~1K each — ~15× less footprint. **Safe where the Room reorder is not:** the catalogue is *reference data*, not instructions, so moving it reorders no instruction relative to another; the Concierge has no safety floor (PM-only); and the rules referencing it (*"never invent a lesson… name ONLY the lessons in that agent's list above"*) stay last. Becomes **Phase 0**, ships independently, with a guard test asserting the prompt head is **byte-identical across two mandates differing in every field** for ≥2 blocks' worth — the property the speedup depends on, silently destroyed by anyone later personalising one line of the head. **Phase 0 dispatched** as lane `CR077-CONCIERGE` (coder.api, `GATE: spawned`) 2026-07-23 after the Architect independently re-measured the mechanism against `192.168.20.74:8000` on a prompt built from scratch: catalogue-last → **0** prefix-cache hit tokens of 29,892 queried, 5,218 ms; catalogue-first, same brand-new user → **29,344** hit tokens, **284 ms** (metrics delta on `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total`). Serving config reproduced exactly (`block_size="2096"`, `_block_size_resolved="True"`, `user_specified_block_size="False"`, `enable_prefix_caching="True"`, `mamba_cache_mode="align"`), and the structural cause confirmed in code — `base` at `concierge_prompts.py:84` is itself mandate-derived, so nothing precedes the catalogue that is shared between users. Phase 2 (Room ANALYSTS parallelisation) **dispatched** as lane `CR077-ROOM` (coder.room, `GATE: independent`) 2026-07-23 after Saiful settled the Room-quality question on evidence: `news_analyst` quoted the Reddit sentiment score (social's domain) **while speaking before social**, so the four analysts draw on one shared data block, not on each other — Architect confirmed structurally (`room_prompts.py:338`, agent-independent profile). Phase 1's A/B **demoted from blocking gate to verification the lane attaches**. Hard condition: strip/rescope the "build on the transcript" line for the concurrent analysts. RESEARCHERS/RISK/VERDICT stay sequential. Phase 3 (`gpu_memory_utilization` 0.5→) **handed to the LLM-host team, not a build-fleet lane** — Saiful: *"we have a team taking care of it. do not touch it"* (2026-07-23). **Phase 0 INTEGRATED 2026-07-27 (AT:R65) at `882b1c9`** — audited **COMPLETE r1** by an Architect-spawned auditor that reproduced the live measurement itself rather than accepting the hand-off: **14,672 hit tokens / 318 ms** on a second user's first message vs **0 / 2,684 ms** old ordering (14,672 = 7x2096, whole-block; the shared-host contamination caveat did not bite — `query_delta == prompt_tokens` exactly on every request). 1 MINOR, non-blocking (a static divider was added to the head, so "only order changed" is slightly imprecise; it changes no instruction/lesson/routing/safety text). Builder died on its $5 cap mid-lane but had committed incrementally (DEF083 mode, nothing lost), and its hand-off misread `GATE: spawned` as "no auditor required" — PROTOCOL.md 4a means an Architect-spawned auditor, which is why one ran. **Phase 2 (`CR077-ROOM`) is AT AUDIT** on rebased tip `aec620c` (rebased onto CR026's room_runner/room_prompts integration per CR026 FLAG 1; both features verified together, suite 1304). | CR106 | 2026-07-28 | **Room result: a graphical Verdict Board + a collapsed transcript, with the user choosing the default.** Saiful, relaying user feedback: *"the long technical result from convene the room \[is not\] good, most users do not want to read too much, so a graphical/iconical response (with the option to look at the full details) might be easier."* **Measured, not a taste call:** `room_screen.dart` renders a completed run as ONE `SingleChildScrollView` of 12 stacked `MarkdownBody` blocks — `_LENGTH_GUIDE` (`room_prompts.py:65-78`) budgets 30–40 sentences ≈ **3,500–6,000 chars ≈ 4–7 phone screens** before the verdict card, `_scrollToBottom()` pins the user to the bottom of it, and there is **no summary, sectioning, collapse or truncation anywhere** (zero `ExpansionTile`/`AnimatedCrossFade` in `mobile/lib`). Two aggravations: the size/entry/stop/target rows render **only `if (isApprove)`** (`:957`), so a PASS is prose and nothing else; and the Journal replay of the same run is strictly worse (`journal_detail_screen.dart:272-308` — no markdown, no metric rows, no hex avatars). No CR/DEF covered this (checked CR001–105, DEF001–130); the original spec anticipated it (`convene_the_room.md:95-105`, the v1.0 "visual deck… console collapsible"), and this CR redirects that from animated theatre to readable summary. **Decided with Saiful:** both modes ship (*"I like the verdict board, but I also like the collapsed transcript… let's give the user the option"* → persisted preference, first run = BOARD); per-agent stance comes from a **backend structured envelope, not a client-side keyword heuristic** (CR038 — a mis-tinted hex is a confident lie about what an agent said, the DEF059 class); and **this round is spec + prototype only, no code**. **Design.** Hero = a hex-marked KPI tile, not a giant hexagon (`hex_clipper.dart:85` records a label clipping inside hex geometry at 1.15 text scale — usable width is 0.724 of the box), covering **five** states incl. the two the current UI mishandles: `NO_VERDICT` (today amber, i.e. reads as a rejection) and `done && verdict == null` (today one bare sentence — an outage must never be shaped like an outcome); REJECT moves amber→red per `colors_motion_rtl.md`. Consensus comb resolves the core tension — tinting agent hexes by stance **violates "family colour is sacred"** — by encoding **stance as ordinal band position and conviction as a hexagonal ring sweep, hue untouched**; opacity/saturation ramps are forbidden (`hexCyan` clears the 4.2:1 floor only above ~70% alpha, *and* `Opacity(0.35)` already means "hasn't spoken yet" at `room_screen.dart:323`), as is a continuous lean axis (asserts precision an LLM-sampled stance can't support). **The comb holds 11 hexes, not 12** — the PM is the hero tile, captioned `THE PM DECIDES — THIS IS NOT A VOTE`, which kills any "consensus %" reading structurally rather than with a disclaimer. Collapsed rows **extract, never summarise**: the first `**bold**` span verbatim (agents are already instructed to bold key metrics by `_PROSE_FORMAT`, so it's a quotation and cannot be wrong), the Trader's level triple via `_LEVEL_PATTERNS`, an amber mark on `content.contains('[AMI')`; first-sentence truncation is **rejected** — Bull/Bear prompts ask for "thesis + evidence + falsifier" and cutting at 32 chars strands the negation. **Three backend gaps gate the pixels:** **B1** `verdict.level_provenance` — `room_runner.py:859-862` MINTS a missing stop/target at `entry*0.94`/`entry*1.13` and discloses it only by appending a sentence to `reason`; clamping that sentence behind a WHY expander *while* promoting the same numbers into a to-scale ribbon with a computed ratio makes an existing DEF059-shaped problem worse, so **no provenance → no ribbon** (side effect: every defaulted verdict is pixel-identical at R:R exactly 2.2:1); **B2** per-agent `{stance, conviction, headline}` envelope on the PM's proven JSON precedent, quantised in the schema, `null` surviving to the pixel (missing → gutter, never `neutral`); **B3** `opinions_not_included` + the `agent_withheld` SSE event, both emitted server-side and silently dropped client-side today. **B2 must land AFTER DEF125** (flat `max_tokens=400` truncates the RM mid-sentence in 66.1% of convenes — an envelope adds tokens), and rebase behind CR098/CR104/CR105, which all edit `room_prompts.py`/`_format_profile`. **Delivered this round:** the spec; a self-contained clickable prototype (`prototype/room_board.html`, 8 scenarios × 2 modes × dark/light × LTR/RTL × 1.0/1.15 text scale, fonts inlined as subsetted base64 woff2 because an Artifact's CSP blocks font CDNs and a silent fallback would mean reviewing the wrong typeface); and `docs/initial_specs/05_design/data_viz_and_meters.md` — the **missing data-viz chapter**, since the design-system mount's entire chart guidance is one line ("blue primary, green positive, red negative") and every chart shipped so far made local decisions. Prototype verification caught two real bugs that would otherwise have shipped: RTL bidi rendered `2.8 : 1` as **`1 : 2.8`** (a wrong number, not a layout nit — hence the LTR-locked ribbon + isolated numeric runs), and using the AA-safe accent *text* tones as *fills* turned the light-mode comb muddy (fills keep their tone, only ink darkens — now two tokens per accent). **Five defects spotted, flagged to the Architect to mint, not filed here:** `NO_VERDICT` renders as a rejection + leaks the raw enum untranslated; `RoomVerdict.fromJson` coerces unknown actions to `PASS`; `ShareService.shareVerdict` takes `isApprove`/`isPass` booleans so REJECT and NO_VERDICT produce identical share cards (and a board gets shared far more than prose); `opinions_not_included`/`agent_withheld` dropped; Journal replay worse than the Room. **SCOPE EXTENDED 2026-07-28 — the Decision Journal replay too.** Saiful: *"we need to implement this also in the journal when we display room results."* That surface is the worse of the two: `journal_detail_screen.dart:272-308` re-renders each contribution as a bare `Text(content)` with **no markdown parsing** (so `_PROSE_FORMAT`'s `**bold**` metrics reach users as literal asterisks), no metric rows and no hex avatars. **One widget, two mappers — not two renderers:** rebuilding the board separately for Room and Journal is DEF098's named class (*two independent renderers of the same data, neither a superset*), which is exactly how the Journal fell behind; extract `RoomBoard`/`RoomTranscriptRows` against a shared view-model and give each screen a mapper. **The Journal payload is a SNAPSHOT, not a `RoomRun`** (`build_journal_entry_for_run`): it carries the full verdict (incl. `opinions_not_included`), transcript and `model_tier`, but **never `duration_ms` or `credit_cost`** — so the strip reads `{TIER} TIER · MANDATE v{n}` there — and `live_data_notice`/`agent_withheld` are stream-only and absent. **Vintage degradation is the design point:** an entry written before a field existed will never have it, and re-fetching `GET /v1/room/{reference_id}` does NOT fix that (`RoomRunRow.verdict` is the same JSONB written in the same moment), so the board degrades **per entry** — no `level_provenance` → metric list, no ribbon, no ratio; no stances → the comb states *"stances were not recorded for this run"* rather than three empty bands; **never backfilled**, since an inferred provenance is a guess about a past decision wearing the authority of a record. Mode B degrades to nothing at all (it needs only `content`), which is why it ships first on that surface. **A journal entry is a record, not a setup:** prototyping caught the board offering `OPEN TRADE TICKET` against a June entry's $118.20 — a one-tap trade at a stale price; the Journal gets `SEE CHART` + `RE-RUN WITH CURRENT MANDATE` (what `screen_inventory.md:120` already specifies) and a `LEVELS AS OF {date} — A RECORD, NOT A CURRENT SETUP` caption. Prototype now carries 8 scenarios across both surfaces incl. a pre-CR106 journal entry showing the degradation live. **AGENT IDENTITY IN THE COMB, 2026-07-28.** Saiful: *"we will need to be able to identify the agents in the voices… since the groups share the icon colours."* Correct, and unfixable by colour: family colour is shared **by design**, so 3 cyan analysts / 2 purple researchers / 3 amber debators are mutually indistinguishable — and BULL vs BEAR, the pair a reader most wants to separate, are the same purple. **Three options built and compared at real size in the prototype (rail control *Hex identity*, kept so the call stays auditable): letters win.** Icons rejected — at 14pt only arrows/chevrons/equals/zigzag survive, the ledger/document/bubble/shield/merge glyphs are mush, and all eleven would make the reader learn a legend for something that already has a name; colour-only rejected because it IS the reported problem. Labels come from a new `combLabel` on `Agent`, capped at 4 chars (`FUND MKT NEWS SOC BULL BEAR RES TRD AGG CON NEU`) — only `RES-M→RES` and `TRADE→TRD` differ from the shipped `abbreviation`, i.e. a truncation, not a second naming scheme; 4-char at 7.5pt tightened, 2–3-char at 9pt, both scaling with text scale, band wraps rather than clips. **Conviction moves from the hexagonal ring to a 22×3pt underline bar** — the ring cost ~9pt of diameter, exactly the room a legible label needs, and given "how strongly" vs "who", **who wins**; length is a weaker magnitude channel than arc but still a magnitude channel, and unknown conviction still renders no bar at all. **Ink is slate900, never white** — measured `Colors.white` on `hexAmber` = **1.8:1** and on `hexGreen` = **2.1:1**, below even the 3:1 large-text floor; dark ink clears 7:1 on all six family fills and serves both themes since fills keep their tone. **Two further shipped defects found while sizing this** (now 7 flagged, not 5): `HexAvatar` sets its label in white on the family fill (live contrast failure on every Risk debator and the Trader, Floor honeycomb + Room transcript), and sizes it at `size*0.16` — 15.4pt on the 96pt Floor hexes it was tuned for but **4.5pt on the 28pt Room-transcript avatar**, i.e. a decorative smudge where a label was intended. Generalised into `data_viz_and_meters.md` §4.4 as a system rule (colour identifies a family, never a member). **SURFACE SHAPE CORRECTED 2026-07-28.** Saiful: *"the groups does not use hex-like design. look at the current journal design. It uses rounded edges rects."* The first prototype pass hex-cut its panels per the design-system mount, which specs `--clip-angle-panel` for cards/modals — but **nothing in `mobile/lib` implements that**: every content surface ships as a rounded rect (`AmiRadii.card` 8, `AmiRadii.sheet` 12 for `_VerdictCard`, same in `AccentCard` and every `journal_detail_screen.dart` block), hex clipping is reserved for **marks and controls** (avatars, chips, toasts, bottom nav, and `ticker_chart.dart:185`'s period toggle at `cornerCut: 8`), and Room CTAs carry no `shape:` override at all so they are Material-3 stadiums. **The app wins over the mount** — the feature lives inside those screens — and it is the better rule anyway: cutting the corners off every card spends the hexagon on chrome and leaves nothing to distinguish the marks that should carry it. Applied throughout; **hexagonal geometry now survives on exactly three things — the agent marks, the hero's outcome mark, and the BOARD|TRANSCRIPT toggle**. Recorded as a system rule in `data_viz_and_meters.md` §4.0, with a flag that `ami_hex_in_flutter.md` should carry the DS-vs-app divergence where the port is documented. **AGENT SELECTION FROM THE BOARD, 2026-07-28.** Saiful asked whether selecting an agent on the Board should switch to Transcript and open that agent's detailed entry. **Half of it — the destination is right, the trigger is not.** A 26pt mark is a casual target; tearing down the whole surface loses the board's scroll position and forces a hunt for the toggle to return; comparison is the *normal* case ("why is BEAR against?" is almost always followed by "what did CON say?" — four round trips under a mode switch); and a content tap must never rewrite a stored view preference. **Resolved: tap → a bottom sheet** carrying the agent's name/phase, `STANCE`/`CONVICTION` chips when known, the full contribution as parsed markdown and the AMI geometry annotation if present, with the board intact behind it — **and the sheet carries the asked-for destination as an explicit action**, `READ THE FULL DEBATE →`, which switches to Transcript, expands that row, scrolls it into view and briefly tints it. The mode switch then happens when the user asks for it, not as a side effect of curiosity. New trap **T-MODESIDE**: only the segmented toggle may call `setMode`; the jump changes mode for the screen only, or one curious tap silently rewrites what every future Room opens as. Withheld/empty agents get **no** jump action (a trip to a row reading `NOT HEARD` is a wasted one); the sheet hosts the same expanded-row widget the transcript uses, so there is still no third renderer (T-TWICE); transcript rows continue to expand in place, so the sheet exists only where the full text has nowhere to go. Sheet discipline per DEF075 — scrollable body, ~72% cap, `sheetBottomInset(mq)`, the guard CR080 flagged `convene_sheet.dart` for missing. **Phased so Phase 1 is shippable alone and covers BOTH surfaces** (shared widget + toggle + hero + collapsed rows + override line + PASS/NO_VERDICT boards on today's data, no ribbon, no comb). `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — 31 proposed ARB ids listed in the spec. Backend: **B1** `verdict.level_provenance` (`pm|trader|ami_default` — three values, because a two-state flag would call the Trader's substituted entry a PM decision) with the prose disclosure KEPT alongside it; **B2** the per-agent stance envelope; **B3** was already delivered by CR098 and re-measured as such rather than rebuilt. **B2 deviates from §4.2's JSON shape, deliberately**: a trailing machine-readable line, not a wrapper, because the PM precedent the CR cites fails to parse in ~22% of runs (DEF058) and there a failure is invisible — an agent's prose IS the product, so a wrapper's failure mode is the user reading raw JSON. A trailing line fails partially into the gutter §3.4 already designed. Client: one `RoomBoard` + `RoomTranscriptRows` over a shared view-model, two mappers in one file, and the acceptance-#10 parity test comparing a 23-field fingerprint across both surfaces — which also closed **DEF143**. **Two documented departures from the spec, both because the spec's own numbers were wrong or its remedy unsafe:** §6 T-UNKNOWN asked for an unrecognised action to render as `NO RESULT`, but that asserts a failure that did not happen, so it renders neutrally with the raw token (CR098 acceptance #9's settled answer); and §3.2's `slate900` comb ink is unusable on `hexPurple` (measured 4.22 vs white's 4.23, `textHigh` 3.85), so the comb hex uses a canvas interior with family-colour ink instead — see **DEF142**, which stays open because `HexAvatar` itself is untouched. **Not shipped:** the peek sheet's tap-to-open is wired but acceptance #14's scroll-position assertion is untested; §7's light-mode and RTL claims are pinned only by the ribbon's LTR lock. 1508 backend + 210 mobile green; 17 mutations verified RED across the three commits. `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — 52 ARB keys added to en/ar/ms. | done | [CR106_room_result_visual_summary/](CR106_room_result_visual_summary/) | AT:R65 |

| CR108 | 2026-07-28 | **Lessons track hexes: wrap the label to two lines (do NOT enlarge the hex).** Saiful: *"maybe we can make the hex bigger and allow two rows. the main size issue is likely in the lessons."* Second half right, first half unnecessary — **measured**: the track hex is already ~143pt wide (`0.40` of available width, the largest hexagon in the app after `agent_unlocked_screen`), and the constraint is *where the label sits*, not hex size. `track_hex_button.dart:43` places it at `y=0.224` — above centre, above the progress doughnut — where a flat-top hexagon is only **0.724** of its box (103.5pt of 143pt), and it is locked to `maxLines: 1, softWrap: false` inside a `FittedBox(scaleDown)` at an 8px base, so a long label does not wrap, it **shrinks**. `ISLAMIC FINANCE` = 15 chars × 0.825em × 8px = 99pt in a 103.5pt box (the 4.7pt of headroom `hex_clipper.dart:85` already records); at 1.15 text scale it needs 113.9pt so FittedBox drops it to **8.4px** — below its own 8px base, and the only label in the set that gets *smaller* when the user asks for bigger text. **Fix:** `maxLines: 2`, `softWrap: true`, cap 8px→10px, and size against the **top line's** width (a two-line block centred on y=0.224 puts line 1 at ≈y=0.176 → 0.676 of the box = 96.7pt, not 0.724) — with the two-line fraction derived as a companion constant beside `flatTopHexWidthFractionAtLabel` so a future y-position change moves both. Only **3 of 13** labels wrap (`NEWS & MACRO`, `ASSET CLASSES`, `ISLAMIC FINANCE`); the other ten stay one line and take the higher cap. **Result: every label 8.0→10.0px at 1.0× (+25%), smallest at 1.15× goes 8.4→10.5px, and nothing shrinks below its base any more.** **Explicitly NOT enlarging the hexagon** — `0.40` is guarded by `honeycomb_layout_test`, and that guard exists because it was once set to `0.80`, rendering every hex at double size and overflowing the column 2×. **Also not in scope:** the CR106 consensus comb (bigger cells + wrapping there is only needed to carry *icons*, which needs ≥44pt cells → 6 per row → the FOR band wraps → ~+100pt of board height; letters at 26pt are already legible per the CR106 prototype and CR107's rule puts the comb below the icon threshold), and icons in the track hex (CR107 §3 keeps lesson *tracks* out of the agent icon program — different entity). Acceptance flags that `honeycombTrackLabel` is hardcoded English with no ARB coverage — the same gap CR107 §1 raises for agent names — so wrapping behaviour for longer AR/MS translations is untested by definition. **RULED (Saiful, 2026-07-29): APPROVED to build, bundled with DEF154 as one mobile-legibility pass.** Not because they share code — CR108 is `track_hex_button.dart` and DEF154 is `hex_avatar.dart`, different widgets on different entities — but because they share a *verification cost*: both change type rendering across many surfaces, both need Saiful's eye on a physical device, and shipping them separately means two builds, two device checks and two TestFlight round-trips for what is one judgement call about whether the lessons screens read properly. **DEF142** is queued on `HexAvatar` too and should be folded into the same pass rather than becoming a third trip. The sequencing consequence is recorded on CR107: that CR is HELD until this pass lands, because DEF154's font floor is the control for whether its icon program is needed at all. Spec: [CR108_lessons_track_label_two_lines/](CR108_lessons_track_label_two_lines/). **ROUND 1 BUILT AND REJECTED — pre-audit, by the Architect (2026-07-29, AT:R65). Nothing reached `main`.** Built on `lane/DEF142.coder.mobile` @ `846e92cd` alongside DEF142; the lane reported 306 green and 27/27 on its own new `track_hex_button_test.dart`. **It does not work, and the test proving it works cannot fail.** Three facts, each measured against the real render tree at the lane's own 143.2×124 fixture. **(1) The wrap never happens.** `FittedBox` lays its child out with *unbounded* constraints, so `softWrap`/`maxLines: 2` can never break a line — `RenderParagraph.size.height` reads **14.0, one line, for all 13 labels**. The new `flatTopHexWidthFractionAtTwoLineLabel` constant is applied to the `SizedBox` *around* the `FittedBox`, never to the text that is supposed to wrap, so the two-line branch is dead code at every geometry rather than just this one. **(2) The labels are therefore still being shrunk — the exact behaviour this CR exists to remove — and five are now SMALLER than before the change**, including `ISLAMIC FINANCE`, the one label the CR is named for: 5.64px → 5.47px, with `ASSET CLASSES`, `FUNDAMENTALS`, `NEWS & MACRO` and `FOUNDATIONS` also regressing. (Relative measurement under `flutter_test`'s fixed-width font — the before/after comparison is valid because both sides share it; the absolute pixel values are **not** a device claim.) The mechanism is font-independent: raising the base 8→10px makes the text 25% wider and the box narrows 103.7→96.8, while the wrap that was meant to absorb that never engages. The four short labels that never scaled (`RISK`, `EDGE`, `QUANT`, `ETHICS`) do get the full raise to 10px — so the change helps the labels that were never the problem and hurts the five that were. **(3) The guard is vacuous.** `paragraph.getTransformTo(null).getMaxScaleOnAxis()` returns **1.000 for every label** — it does not observe `RenderFittedBox`'s paint-time scale — while the painted rect proves real scaling is happening (`ISLAMIC FINANCE`: paragraph 177.0px, painted 96.8px). So `_renderedLabelFontSize` computes a constant and all 26 size assertions reduce to `expect(10.0, greaterThanOrEqualTo(10.0))`. **Proven by mutation: setting `needsTwoLines = false` — deleting the entire feature — leaves all 27 tests green.** The lane's own comment reasons correctly about why reading `Text.style.fontSize` would be wrong, then substitutes a second metric that is also blind and never validates it against a known-scaled case; `tester.getRect(finder).width / RenderParagraph.size.width` is the metric that works, because `localToGlobal` applies the paint transform. Also measured: **9 of 13** labels exceed the one-line box at this fixture, not the "exactly 3" the hand-off claimed — nothing depends on the count, since none of the nine actually wrap, but it shows the claim was reasoned from the three labels this row discusses rather than measured across the set. **Re-laned as round 2, Part B only** (`orchestration/dispatch/lanes/DEF142.assign.md`), with the bounded-text fix, the corrected metric, a `paraH` two-line assertion, an explicit decision for the unbreakable-word case (`FUNDAMENTALS`, 12 characters, cannot wrap at any width and must fall back to scaling), and a **mandatory** mutation showing the new assertions RED. **DEF142's Part A is accepted and untouched by this** — its census floor and contrast extension are sound and its own mutation goes RED. **CR107 stays HELD**: it was waiting on this pass as its control, and the control is not yet valid. **ROUND 2 BUILT (coder.mobile, AT:R65, 2026-07-30) — the mechanism, not just the metric, was wrong; both are fixed now.** Round 1 wrapped the `Text` in a `FittedBox`, which always lays its child out with *unbounded* constraints, so `softWrap`/`maxLines: 2` never had a width to break against. The fix moves the bound: the two-line branch now gives the `Text` its width from a plain `SizedBox` (no `FittedBox` at all), so real line breaks happen; `FittedBox` is kept only for the single-line branch, which is the half of the mechanism that already worked pre-CR108. Whether a candidate wraps is now *confirmed*, not assumed — `TextPainter(maxLines: 2, maxWidth: twoLineBox).computeLineMetrics()` must return >1 line with every line's width inside the box, or the label falls back to the single-line `FittedBox` scale-down path instead. **The unbreakable-word case, measured rather than assumed:** the round-2 assign named `FUNDAMENTALS` (12 characters, no space) as unable to wrap and required an explicit fallback decision for it — measured against the real render tree, that premise does not hold. Flutter's default line breaker splits an unbreakable "word" at the character level as a last resort when `maxLines` allows a further line (UAX#14 fallback), so `FUNDAMENTALS` wraps into e.g. `FUNDAMENT`/`ALS` and meets the floor at full size like every other label — it never reaches the fallback branch. That branch is still real and load-bearing; a synthetic 36-character single "word" (`SUPERCALIFRAGILISTICEXPIALIDOCIOUSXX`, no shipped label is this long) proves it triggers correctly (`geometricScale` 0.24, one line, not two). **The metric, replaced and validated before being trusted:** round 1's `paragraph.getTransformTo(null).getMaxScaleOnAxis()` does not observe `RenderFittedBox`'s paint-time scale and reads `1.000` unconditionally — reproduced directly in the new test file, not just asserted in prose. The replacement, `tester.getRect(finder).width / RenderParagraph.size.width` (goes through `localToGlobal`, which does apply the paint transform), is validated against a harness forced to a known 0.5× `FittedBox` scale before being used on the real widget. A `paraH` assertion (`RenderParagraph.size.height` two line-heights, using a same-harness single-line label as the reference rather than a bare `TextPainter` — the ambient `MaterialApp`/`Scaffold` `DefaultTextStyle` merges in a `height` the bare painter never sees) makes a silently-unwrapped label a visible failure, which round 1's assertions could not produce. **Mutation, mandatory this round:** reverting to round 1's `FittedBox`-wraps-`Text` structure turns 21 of 31 assertions RED, including the new `paraH`, `geometricScale`, and metric-sanity checks — restoring the fix returns all 31 to green. **Re-measured against the `8bb00594` baseline** (the pre-CR108 8px single-line-only mechanism), all 13 labels, at both 1.0× and 1.15× text scale, using the corrected metric on both sides: every label is equal to or larger than its baseline, none regresses (`ISLAMIC FINANCE` 5.64→10.0 at 1.0×, 5.78→11.5 at 1.15×; `FUNDAMENTALS` 7.05→10.0 at 1.0×, 7.23→11.5 at 1.15×; the other 11 similarly non-decreasing) — full table in the hand-off. Full mobile suite green (382, up from the pre-merge 306 — `main` gained other lanes' tests in the interim), `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` exit 0, the same 5 pre-existing infos named in the assign. **Not independently verified against a physical device** — GATE is independent; this is coder.mobile's own measurement, pending audit. | CR109 | 2026-07-30 | **[HIGH PRIORITY — Saiful] The Game: a P&L competition in AMI Cash, separate from the training sim.** Saiful: *"This is a new game. Specifically designed for P&L of your AMI CASH. Measured only by the win/loss during the game period"* — weekly / monthly / quarterly / 6-month / annual — plus *"career points (for personal satisfactions)"*, a restart when *"you have lost too much"*, and *"when you re-start, the points you've lost will still hit your career points"*. **Depends on CR133 (bottom-nav restructure) and must be developed with it** — CR109 assumes the game has a home in the shell but deliberately does not say where; §13.1 records why sequencing them apart fails (the game ships with nowhere to live, or the nav ships with an empty tab). **Also depends on CR134 (design conformance review, AT:UI Designer): the game screens ship in CR134's corrected patterns, not the drafted ones** — hex geometry for controls (not rounded rects), colour by agent-family not literal-cyan CTAs, fill/dash provenance encoding (never opacity/saturation dimming), mirror surfaces stay colour-neutral (no amber scold), and ceremony motion is a bounded ≤600ms one-time draw-on rather than continuous animation. CR134 found zero hexagons across all 20 mocked screens and no design criterion anywhere in §19's ~60 acceptance items; its §3 criteria are folded in as new §19/§21 acceptance below, laning does not proceed on the drafted screens as-is. **Amendment A — no longer additive:** *"remove the current (boring!) reputation game"* — replaces `reputation_service.py` + `league_service.py` + `league_screen.dart` + badges + streaks, which scored process only (`lesson_passed: 5`, `room_verdict: 3`) and stated *"no P&L-linked event exists or ever will"*, so today a user can top the weekly league without their portfolio ever making money. Folds in CR063's in-app rules surface; **CR063 and CR093 close as stale**. Data left untouched, no migration — *"We are in Alpha. No real users yet"*. **Amendment B — Saiful rejected round 1 as a game: *"we only have a design, not a game design."*** Diagnosis: **five concurrent windows over one NAV curve is not five games, it is one game reported five times** — one set of decisions, five scores, no separate strategy or tension per cadence. **Amendment C — *"concentrate on making CR109 bullet proof… How do you propose all the game elements will fit? You need to have the full design."*** Navigation removed and reassigned to CR133 (it was scope creep into a change with its own blast radius); the organising model added; and the gaps a scoring spec leaves now filled. **THE SPINE — a three-layer model with a one-way rule.** Layer 1 **the Stake** (AMI Cash, positions, NAV — resets every entry); layer 2 **the Contest** (TWR, field, rank, placement `p` — collapses at close); layer 3 **the Record** (career points, titles, flair, cosmetics — never resets). **Value flows UP, never DOWN.** This is not a slogan: it *derives* the choices that otherwise look arbitrary — flat 10,000 capital for everyone (the Record can't buy Stake), cosmetic-only rewards (the Record can't buy Contest advantage), tokens refused (money is a fourth layer outside the game; paying in makes the Record convertible, paying out makes Stake purchasable), % TWR never absolute AMI Cash (else a bigger Stake buys rank and plan tier is pay-to-win), placement not raw return (raw return leaks *market conditions* into the Record, recording *when* you played not how well), and day-one competitiveness (a new player has a full Stake and an empty Record, and the Record never enters the Contest). The title multiplier is the one element that looks like a downward flow and isn't — it multiplies **within** layer 3, so scores compound with seniority while two players in a field always face identical conditions. **A run is an entry, not an account** — 10,000 AMI Cash fresh at entry, same at every cadence, own open/close/board; everyone starts dead equal on day one, the mid-period-join problem vanishes, every run has a natural ceremony boundary. Entry closes at the bell; **entry is free and always will be — an entry fee is *consideration*, one of the three legs of the gambling test**. **One live run per cadence** (answering *"can you enter multiple long term games?"* — no: the `+100`/`−40` curve makes parallel entries strictly +EV, so 12 rolling Annuals played maximally aggressive is a farm). **Full run/entry state machines** (`ANNOUNCED→ENTRY_OPEN→LOCKED→LIVE→SETTLING→CLOSED→ARCHIVED`, plus `ABANDONED` when a demand-gated field never fills, and `ENTERED→ACTIVE→FINISHED|FORFEIT|VOID`), scoring idempotent at close. **Trade rules were never specified and contained a live exploit:** `sim_engine.submit()` fills at the current quote whenever called, so outside US market hours a player trades against a stale last price *already knowing what happened after it* — harmless in training, a time machine in a scored contest. **Fills only during market hours; out-of-hours orders queue to the next open.** Explicitly NOT covered by the no-rules decision, because it is the difference between simulating a market and simulating one with hindsight. Also settled: long-only (`sim_engine` models no short), market orders, fractional allowed, cash earns nothing (interest would reward sitting out), no leverage ever, open positions marked not liquidated at close. **Thin fields — the most serious hole, from Saiful (*"on a new platform, we may find a month with a single player!"*):** `p=(n−rank)/(n−1)` is **undefined at n=1** and a coin flip at n=2; **a field of one pays the game's largest prize for beating nobody**; and rolling starts **break the very property that justifies placement** (§6.2 chose it because everyone in a field faced the same market), so merging cohorts across start dates — the obvious first idea — cannot work. Fixed by demand-gated rolling starts, **benchmark-relative career points below the placement threshold** (`alpha = TWR − benchmark`, preserving the exact market-cancellation property placement was chosen for, working at n=1, needing **no new infra** since `current_history()` serves SPY with a source flag and `portfolio_stats.beta()` ships), and titles requiring a real field. Degrades loudly: *"Field of 3. Scored against the S&P 500, not against the field."* **This is the DEFAULT path at alpha field sizes, not a fallback** — ships in phase 1 or phase 1 ships a divide-by-zero. **Rewards (Saiful: *"What do they get for being Champion?"*)** fall out of the one-way rule: **competition rewards are never purchasable and purchasable things are never competition rewards** (a trophy you can buy isn't a trophy, and it would give the Record a market price), and **no reward may improve future performance** (else the game compounds toward whoever won early). Tokens refused. Density scales inversely with cadence frequency — 52 weekly champions a year can't all get something permanent: weekly gets points only, monthly a badge, **quarterly a displayed title riding your handle on every board next quarter** (temporary but *worn*, the strongest cheap reward), half permanent flair + agent frame, annual a never-expiring title + agent skin + **a plaque in the Room** + Champions invitational. **Agent cosmetics are the best reward idea but there is no art** — `mobile/assets/` has zero portraits, agents render as icons + a resolved accent — so a skin means `accent + hex frame + material treatment`, which the design system already generates programmatically: zero art cost, on-brand. **What the other 25 get matters more than the champion prize** (one winner in 26 = twenty-five got nothing = churn): every close yields a progress marker where one is true. Free win: `BadgeRow.is_permanent_flair` exists from CR092 and `GET /v1/league/badges` ships live with **zero Flutter reading it**. **Edge cases specified:** field never fills, field of 1–2, halted/delisted mid-run, **anonymous→claimed mid-run (`merge_service.py` does NOT re-key `BadgeRow`/`StreakFreezeRow` today — a pre-existing gap that would strand a player's record at the exact moment they create an account; this CR must fix its own tables)**, account deleted mid-run, container restart mid-settlement, US-market-time boundaries. **NO ARENA RULES — Saiful's call, reaffirmed after argument:** the game path skips `check_mandate_compliance` entirely — no position/sector/drawdown cap, no cooldown, **and no halal / locale / long_only screen** (the halal screen is `if c.halal:` at `safety_floor.py:289`, inside that same function). **Accepted risk recorded the way D-060 was: a halal-only user trades unscreened on a scored path.** Obligations that aren't gates: the entry surface must **disclose** it (a screen that silently stops existing is the CR040 failure mode) and the training safety floor stays mandatory. **The split is load-bearing:** `sim_engine.py:607-640` already hard-rejects mandate breaches (so round 1's concentration risk was *overstated*), but `MandateRow` is keyed on `user_id` and Settings can edit it, so **on a shared account loosening your own mandate is a win-the-game move**; and `resolve_mandate` falls back to a **client-supplied** `mandate_override` while the mandate row is only created at claim, so an anonymous player supplies their own rules. **Ceremony:** entries-close countdown, the bell, one rank beat per US close (never per tick — that's a slot machine), the final stretch, a **settlement freeze** withholding results ~1h, the full-screen Close, the permanent record + share card, a dignified **Wind-Up** so a blowup is a chapter not a fail screen, and multi-category **Annual Awards** (more categories = more winners). Plus a **notification matrix** — and **push does not exist**, the only trace repo-wide being `note="TODO B1: fire APNs push notification here"` (`room.py:134`), so the anticipation layer is inert until its own CR. **Infra blocker, D-060's own third objection still literally true: no NAV/equity-curve/snapshot table exists in `models.py`.** `portfolio_nav_daily` must be append-only, user-scoped and **must NOT FK to `sim_portfolios`** — `reset_portfolio()` hard-deletes the portfolio and every `SimTradeRow`, so a FK cascades the game's history away; key on `user_id`+`run_id`. **Compliance is why this is not laned:** four documents forbid it — `roadmap.md:138`, **D-060** (`decision_log.md:302`), `daily_and_streaks.md`, `competition_rules.md` v1.0 §8 — and CR064 bound the zero-P&L rule as *a binding invariant, not a design note* because the store's "simulated gambling: No" answer depends on it. Mapped against the three-leg test: **consideration absent by design** (free entry), **prize absent by design** (cosmetic, non-purchasable), leaving **chance-vs-skill** as the live question — which the no-rules decision pushes toward chance at short cadences and cadence weighting pushes back on. Awarding credits on a P&L outcome is the step that needs the lawyer. **Phased as thin slices, because the monster is smaller than it looks:** at alpha field sizes the entire Contest layer is nearly inert — every field sits below the placement threshold, so runs score against the benchmark anyway, which makes **cohorts, demand gating, the placement curve, titles and the multiplier scale features rather than launch features** (building them first builds machinery that cannot run). Slice 1 (NAV table + tick + `twr.py` + the equity curve on the *training* portfolio) and slice 2 (game portfolios, entry, the game trade path, restart, the merge fix) carry **zero compliance surface**, so engineering starts while the legal work runs in parallel; slice 3 (scoring pass + benchmark scoring + career ledger + the Close) is the **first playable game**; slice 4 (the open board, placement, titles) turns on when fields clear n≥8. **The volume is not the risk — the coupling is:** CR109+CR133 can be *developed* together and *shipped* apart, with the game living behind the Floor card until CR133's destination exists. Implementation package ready for laning — schema DDL, API contracts, module boundaries, the fence against reusing the training submit path (**no `skip_compliance` flag** — extract shared mechanics and keep two public entry points, so the difference is structural per CR040), lane split and a 21-row test matrix: [implementation_plan.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/implementation_plan.md). **Playability reviewed** ([playability_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/playability_review.md)) against *"will this game be easy to start? will it be addictive? what brings back the player"* — verdict: coherent but **not yet playable**, and the worst flaw was self-inflicted. **Dead start (defect-grade, now fixed in §4):** entry-closes-at-the-bell plus fixed calendar starts meant a player arriving Tuesday could not enter until the following Monday — first experience of the headline feature was *"come back in six days."* Fixed by **rolling starts at every cadence** (weekly fields open every trading day, monthly weekly, Q/H/Y on the demand gate); everyone inside a field still starts the same day, so same-clock fairness is untouched. **Verified engagement risk: this CR deletes the app's only daily-return mechanic** — `streak()` lives in `reputation_service.py:271`, which Amendment A removes, and the game's heartbeat is *weekly*; recommended fix is to re-home a streak onto **runs finished / periods entered** rather than check-ins (a query over `game_entries`, not a subsystem). **The game is also the app's *unsupported* mode** — training has 12 agents and a safety floor, the game deliberately has neither yet is scored and permanent, so a beginner's first game action is "pick a stock" with no help and real consequences; gating first entry behind a training milestone is recommended but needs Saiful's call. Also flagged: ~5 days to first feedback with an empty day 0, and a first close that at alpha reads *"1st of 3, scored against the S&P"* — deflating, so §8.4's progress markers move from slice 8 to slice 3. Hooks ranked honestly, with the uncomfortable note that the strongest one (open positions / loss aversion) is the psychology the curriculum exists to warn about — which is why §10's *one beat per market close, never per tick* rule matters more than it looks. **DUELS BROUGHT BACK (Saiful: *"I really like the Dual….. how can we bring it back?"*) — as slice 3b, sequenced BEFORE the open board, because the review's central finding inverts their position:** the open board needs `n ≥ 8` to mean anything and every alpha field is below that, so the flagship competitive surface is inert exactly when the product most needs players to feel something — **a duel needs `n = 2`**, making it the only competitive format that works at launch, and it turns the first close from *"1st of 3, scored against the S&P"* into *"you beat VECTOR_11 by 1.4%."* Two constraints: **head-to-head scoring carved out of both existing paths** (never the placement curve, since at `n = 2` `p` is exactly 1.0 or 0.0 and the winner would take the largest award in the game; never the benchmark path either, since `n = 2` is intended here rather than a shortfall), and **auto-matched only at MVP** — anonymous-first onboarding makes alt accounts nearly free, so direct challenge-by-handle is a trivial collusion farm (make an alt, throw the duel, bank the win); auto-matching removes the ability to choose your victim, closing it structurally rather than by detection. **House desks (Saiful: *"we can run 'bot' players to make up the league, and we can have the bot players challenge the real players for a duel"*)** — the answer to what scoring alone cannot fix: §6.6 keeps the *numbers* honest in a thin field but cannot make a board feel alive or supply a duel opponent when no other human is online. They fill the board at every cadence, issue declinable rate-limited duel challenges, win duels sometimes (an opponent that always loses teaches nothing), and count toward career points. **Disclosure was chosen undisclosed, then REVERSED by Saiful on his own argument:** *"if we do not disclose that it's a bot, then if the copy happens (and it can happen off app) the user is copying what they thought is a person!"* — the decisive framing, sharper than the licensing objection that preceded it: the harm is that **the user's belief about the source is false** (they think they are copying a person who knows something, not a strategy that did well), and once a result leaves the app in a screenshot there is no disclosure surface left. So desks compete under **published strategy names** — Momentum Desk, Index Desk, Dividend Desk — never the word "bot", because a *desk* reads as a rival worth beating. Disclosure buys four things: copying becomes **education** (Saiful's *"I would copy the bots trading!"* is the feature working once the rule is published — studying a stated method, not chasing an anonymous winner, which is what `rejected_features_register.md` rejects); it removes the **advice exposure** of a hidden house account whose trades users follow from an entity not licensed to give investment advice; it **dissolves the title tell** Saiful spotted (*"it would be a bit of a give-away if they can be seen winning, but did not win title"* — an exclusion you can observe advertises what it conceals, but with disclosure "house desks are ranked but do not hold titles" is simply a rule); and it **lets them enter every cadence**, where the undisclosed variant would have had to stay out of Quarter/Half/Annual to avoid that tell — precisely the fields that are thinnest and stay thin longest. **Integrity line, separate from and harder than disclosure: a desk's P&L is never generated, sampled or tuned to look plausible.** Desks run real rule-based strategies against real prices through the same game trade path, because desk results feed real users' career points — a fabricated return would land in a real person's permanent Record, the DEF059 shape and exactly the silent-fallback failure CR040 exists to prevent. Roster includes a **concentrated** desk deliberately: a roster of only diversified strategies produces a suspiciously narrow spread, and real fields have blowups. Fill-to-target-field-size so desks taper as real entrants arrive, plus a kill switch and exclusion from every real-user metric (joining the existing CR035-synthetics filter) — a desk must never inflate a number Saiful uses to decide. **Eligibility clause (Saiful: *"we can say that employees and the family of AMI Trading cannot win awards etc"*, then *"you are 'my employee' at this time"* — which collapses it into one rule rather than a list):** **anything operated by, employed by, or affiliated with AMI Trading may rank, but may not hold a title, champion reward or permanent flair.** Four instances of that single principle — house desks (entrants the company operates), the operator himself and staff/admin, household and immediate family, and test/UAT/seed accounts (the Hermes rig on melehost drives a real device and its runs can enter fields). Needed **independently of the desks**, because the operator plays: *"2026 Annual Champion: Saiful"* is a problem whether or not he earned it, and a competition whose operator can win its own prizes looks rigged even when it isn't — which strengthens `competition_rules.md` §8's skill-vs-chance footing. **Ineligible ≠ invisible, and that distinction is the point:** they enter, trade and rank, the board shows what actually happened, and only the *title* passes down to the highest eligible entrant — stated plainly (*"Title: SLATE_07 (2nd overall)"*) rather than silently renumbering, since a board that quietly promotes second place looks like a bug while one that explains itself looks like a rule. This is also what avoids the tell: no hidden exclusion to notice. Scope is deliberately narrow — career points still accrue, so the operator can dogfood progression and desks still populate a meaningful spread. Belongs in **`competition_rules.md` v2.0**, the document with standing, which §15 already re-versions for the P&L change. **Forward dependency: if credits are ever paid on a P&L outcome, operator and staff participation stops being hygiene and becomes load-bearing** — same lawyer review. **FINAL REVIEW** ([final_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/final_review.md)), covering Saiful's last three asks — *"make this addictive… remind them to play… players will be a source of income if they view adverts… enable the social aspect, they can discuss trades and give tips"* — each of which collides with something already decided. **ADS: the trap that would break §15.** The compliance position rests on **consideration absent** (free entry) + **prize absent** (cosmetic, non-purchasable); **rewarded video — the standard mobile pattern — attacks the consideration leg**, and every natural ad-funded mechanic is fatal: *"watch an ad to restart"* makes restart purchasable with attention, *"watch an ad for a second entry"* also breaks §4.1's one-run-per-cadence farm guard, *"watch an ad for extra AMI Cash"* is money buying Stake. Non-monetary consideration counts. **New invariant: no ad may ever be required, rewarded, or gate anything** — not entry, re-entry, restart, capital, information, timing, or cosmetics that double as competition rewards. **The §3.1 one-way rule catches all of them unaided**, the clearest evidence yet that the three-layer model is load-bearing rather than descriptive. Ads therefore run as **ambient inventory on non-contest surfaces** (lobby, Record, app open) — never the board, never the trade ticket, and **never the Close**, since an ad in the trophy moment cheapens the one emotional payoff the period arc exists to deliver; the game monetises **indirectly** by driving sessions. **No ad infrastructure exists** (no SDK, units, mediation or consent flow — "Floor Pass" is a tier name, not an implementation), so ads are **their own CR** and must not be entangled with this schedule. **RETENTION: remind on events that need a decision, never on events that only invite watching** — entries closing / run closing / a challenge received / results ready / dropped out of the top 10 *once per run*, but never "your position moved". Not restraint for its own sake: **the cheap notification costs the valuable one**, because push fatigue makes users disable the channel that delivers the Close. Caps ≤1/day, ≤4/week, quiet hours; lands on the same side as §10's *one beat per market close, never per tick*. **SOCIAL: the app has zero UGC today** — the only user-authored value is the system-generated handle, and there is **no report, no block, no profanity filter, no moderation tooling** anywhere in the repo. **Apple Guideline 1.2 requires four things of any UGC app** (filter, report, block, published contact with **action within 24 hours**) — a standing daily obligation for a one-person team, and the real cost of the feature; an unmoderated stock-tip channel is also the highest-risk UGC category (pump schemes, "DM me for signals" funnels, unlicensed advice on a platform not licensed to give investment advice, and AR/MS content Saiful cannot personally moderate). Phased **A → B → C**: structured reactions (fixed vocabulary, **no moderation surface at all**), then **post-close rationale notes on your own already-closed trades** — the safest reading of "discuss trades" because it is structurally **retrospective** (never a signal), **scoped to your own trades** (never a generic tip channel), **length-capped** and **attached to a real scored decision** (analysis, not opinion) — then open discussion only with a moderation budget that does not exist. **The "tips" itch is already largely served**: the strategy desks publish their rules, and the 12 agents are a licensed-safe, moderation-free way to comment on a closed field. **AMENDMENT D — the independent review fold-in.** Saiful commissioned a review series (`AT:Fable`, five documents: [psychology_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/psychology_review.md) F1–F9, [comparative_review.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/comparative_review.md) C1–C6, [trade_execution_addendum.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/trade_execution_addendum.md) the fee + G1–G3, [playability_addendum.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/playability_addendum.md) the lab framing + L1–L6, [review_synthesis.md](CR109_pnl_game_ami_cash/review_synthesis.md) S1–S10) *"before I commit to a HUGE development cost"*; the series deliberately left CR109.md unedited so the design keeps one author, and this amendment applies it. **Every item's disposition is in §20.** **Two rulings from Saiful.** (1) **The PDT-style day-trade rule is REJECTED; the escalator is held in reserve** — the review framed a 3-round-trips-per-5-days cap as *"realism, not restriction"*, but PDT is a **broker constraint on one account type** (a cash account isn't subject to it), so it fails the bar market-hours and trading-costs clear, and the addendum proposing it opens *"nothing below caps what a player may do"* then caps what a player may do two sections later. The FPL-style escalator (first N fills at base cost, beyond N at 3×) achieves the same anti-scalping goal by **pricing rather than prohibiting**, which is the doctrine. (2) **The agent post-mortem SHIPS, for paying customers only** — amending *"Games is only about trade"* at the close boundary only (the agents stay out of the run itself, which is what that decision protected). It gives the game a direct revenue line that never touches the ad invariant, and puts the strongest upsell in the product at peak attention. **Four fences:** free players keep the **entire** Close (rank, delta, curve, both counterfactual lines — nothing removed to manufacture the upsell, or the peak-end payoff becomes a paywall and the re-entry keystone dies for the half of the base that funds ad revenue); the locked card lives in the **debrief panel, never inside the three-beat ceremony**; retrospective-only is **structural** — a fixed template filled from computed run data, not a prompt instruction (CR038: agents ignore emphatic instructions ~70% of the time); and **no paid feature may alter a run's inputs, scoring or ranking** (§3.1.1 — post-close explanation is the entire permitted surface for plan tier, and the lawyer sees this paragraph rather than discovering it). **FOUR CORRECTIONS TO THE REVIEW, made as its recipient.** (1) **F1 understates itself.** The review found the median player's Record flatlines — placement is zero-sum, so a player oscillating between the 40th and 60th percentile nets ≈0 per run forever (p=0.60→+8.9, p=0.45→−4) and the 500-point first title never arrives. Correct, but §6.5 clamped the **headline**, not the ledger — so the player carries an **invisible debt** (signed total −30, earns +8, screen doesn't move) and when it does move it moves on a ≈zero-drift walk, which is **variable-ratio reinforcement on a status number** — the exact pattern the review's own dark-pattern register marks *never*. **Fix: clamp the ledger at write time**, so `SUM(delta)` is always the displayed number. The wound itself is fixed by a **finish stipend** (~5/weekly finish, guarded on entered + ≥1 trade + not forfeited + held to close, so it can't become a check-in). (2) **S1 and S2 are one mechanism, and it taxes the wrong cohort.** The fee is scoring-**neutral** under placement (everyone in the field pays it, ranks unchanged) and scoring-**negative** under the benchmark (the index pays nothing) — and thin fields route to the benchmark, so the fee **systematically penalises the alpha-window cohort and stops penalising anyone once fields clear n≥8**: same skill, worse score, decided by join date. Fixed by scoring against the **achievable benchmark** (SPY net of the one entry fee a player would pay to hold it — runs end marked not liquidated, so it's one fill) while the Close still **displays** the gross comparison, which is the game's best line: *"the index pays no fees. You beat it anyway"* — the reason most active managers underperform, discovered in the player's own numbers. (3) **F5's arithmetic contradicts F1's.** A 100-point first rung at a 5-point stipend is **twenty finishes** — five months, worse than the problem; raising the stipend instead breaks its own anti-farm guard. **Fix: the first rung is a milestone — 3 finished runs, none forfeited** — reachable in three weeks, unfarmable because it fires once, and it removes a tuning constant instead of adding one. (4) **C1 reopens F1's wound.** Points-capped private fields give zero progression to players in the genre's most retentive mode. **Fix: placement points capped, finish stipend still pays** — placement is rank-dependent so alts can farm it; the stipend is rank-dependent on nothing, so no arrangement between accounts can conjure one. **ACCEPTED FROM THE SERIES.** **The trading cost** (Saiful: *"we have to have some fee attached to the trade… so that 'spray and pray', while may still work, is not the preferred strategy"*) — 10 bps of notional, min 1.00 AMI Cash, per fill, both sides, **burned never pooled** (a pool is a wagered stake and §15's prize leg dies), game path only, desks pay identical costs, **not a capital event** so it doesn't break the TWR chain. bps handles churning big, the minimum handles spraying dust. **Queue-first is promoted to a primary design principle** — US regular hours are **evening in the Gulf and past midnight in Malaysia**, so for the target markets placing orders outside market hours is what most players do most of the time: *plan the book tonight, fills at the open, the morning card reports what filled*. The **3-tap ticket** (watchlist chips → size chips with 25% as the visual default → confirm card showing est. cost and book-percentage), with stop/target presets that are nearly free (`submit()` already accepts them and `evaluate_outcomes()` already watches them) and teach plan-the-exit-at-entry. **The alpha→points formula, which existed in no document** despite being the default path for months at alpha field sizes: same 2.5:1 asymmetry as placement, clamped at ±1 so no alpha outcome outpays winning a field. **The Close gets a ceremony budget of three beats** — the series had attached eleven blocks to the one screen whose entire job is a single emotional payoff, so: the result, **one** insight chosen by priority, the way back in; everything else one tap deeper in a debrief panel. **Entry stays one screen, three taps** for the same reason from the other end. **The re-entry CTA is the final beat** of both Close and Wind-Up, and `close → re-entry` + `first-run activation` are instrumented from day one as the game's health metrics. **The first run is always a duel against the Index Desk** — a routing rule over machinery already planned, giving a guaranteed opponent at n=1 real players, a guaranteed narrative (*you beat the market* or *the market beat you*, both stories), and bounded difficulty for a beginner's first unbounded stock-pick. **Private fields with a join code** — the largest gap the comparison found: two decades of paper-trading competitions and season-long fantasy run on the **private league**, not the public board, and every competitive surface here faced strangers. **The PR board** (best weekly TWR, best alpha, best drawdown control, longest hold, longest streak) — the only competitive surface that **works at n=1**, which is precisely the alpha condition. **A rolling skill stat** on the Record (trailing-N alpha or Sharpe) because career points confound skill with volume and never answer *am I getting better* — it can fall, which is what makes it credible, and it never gates anything. **The streak gets a bye week** (Duolingo's freeze — a long streak's loss becomes a churn cliff). **The mirrors** (lab framing, Saiful: *"this is where you try things and go wild, and see that the wider you go, the less likely you are to make money"*): intent tag, wildness index, two counterfactual lines at every close (*"if you'd held your first picks untouched: +2.1%"*, *"if you'd just held the S&P: +0.6%"*), a live book-heat gauge, and opt-in challenge cards that pay **markers, never points**. All **private** — asserted at the serializer — because billboarding them turns self-knowledge into performance. **This inverts the D-060 objection:** the game doesn't teach gambling psychology, it **falsifies it with the player's own data**. **Attribution on the daily beat** (*"NVDA drove +1.9% of your +2.3%"*) because a no-rules weekly arena is substantially luck and players who sense outcomes aren't contingent on their decisions stop playing — learned helplessness is the churn nobody exit-surveys. **Near-miss framing points up only, never at a loss** (the slot-machine pattern). **Three engine gaps formalised:** dividends unmodelled (so the benchmark is **price-only** to match, with crediting before Q/H/Y — the Dividend Desk is otherwise handicapped by its entire yield), splits unhandled (adjust quantity and basis in place, flag the row, **no TWR break** — a 4:1 split otherwise craters a scored run), and quote freshness (measure Yahoo's lag on melehost before any board is live; the fee raised the exploit's bar to ~20 bps per round trip, so it's due diligence rather than urgent). **All twelve scoring constants move into `games_scoring.py`**, each with a loud test, and §18's tuning list is **generated from it** rather than maintained by hand across five documents. **Staged funding with evidence gates** — Stage 1 (the addictive core: slices 1–3c plus the above) is roughly a third of the plan and contains every hook that matters; **Gate 1** (activation + re-entry meeting targets Saiful sets **before** the build, so it can't be argued backwards from the data) precedes funding slice 4; **Gate 2** (fields clearing n≥8 organically, title rungs being crossed) precedes Q/H/Y, cosmetics and roadmap modes — because **status systems only pay once there is a crowd to hold status in**, and the crowd is built by the cheap loop. **The one-way rule survived intact** — ~40 additions across five documents and not one crosses it, which is the third time §3 has caught a problem unaided. **New risk registered:** paid coaching on a scored board is a **perception** risk even though it is not pay-to-win — two players enter on identical terms and only one is coached afterwards; the mitigation is that the free Close is complete and the boast the game is built around (*beat the market*) needs no subscription to earn. Adds a new user-facing string set — `retranslate:[ar,ms]`. **AMENDMENT F — THE DARK LAUNCH (2026-08-09). This is the amendment that starts the build.** Saiful: *"We have a CR dedicated towards a games engine for the app. I want to start developing it but I do not want to incorporate it into the app just yet, or at least I do not want the users to be able to play it yet."* Two options evaluated — **a separate app** or **hidden access inside AMI Trade** — and he took the second. **Why not a separate app:** the repo has one Flutter package and one bundle ID (`ai.agenticmarketintel.amiTrade`), and the game reuses auth, AMI Cash, quotes, the design system, the API client, i18n, RevenueCat and OneSignal — so a second app either duplicates `mobile/lib/services/` + `mobile/lib/theme/` or forces a shared-package refactor across the tree; it adds a permanent per-release tax (second store record, provisioning, listings, privacy labels, review cycle, and `build_testflight.sh`/`publish_playstore.sh`/`install_iphone.sh` all assume one app); it needs cross-app identity because career points belong to the AMI Trade account; and it is thrown away when the game ships in-app. **Decisively, it does not isolate the half that carries the risk** — the game shares users, AMI Cash, Postgres and market data, so the schema, the migrations and the §7.1 `sim_engine.submit()` split land in the live Alpha stack either way. Saiful then added *"the main app will continue to be developed at the same time"*, which strengthens the ruling rather than complicating it: a fork of the design system would diverge daily instead of costing once. **Four rulings.** (1) **The gate is compile-time, on the client, and it is the ONLY gate.** `bool.fromEnvironment('AMI_GAMES')` guards a const-conditional entry in `mobile/lib/app.dart`'s `routes:` map — the `/dev-preview` pattern already shipped in the app, a registered route with no UI entry point anywhere — so **no distributed binary contains a reachable route**. Structural rather than a runtime flag, because App Review guideline 2.3.1 names hidden/undocumented features and CR040's doctrine is that a switch someone can flip is not a control. Saiful **rejected** a server-side kill switch and user allowlist — *"why bother? so long as no one can reach it, the additional control adds complication with no upside"* — and he is right: a `GAMES_ENABLED` pinned `true` for the entire dark phase is a config line, not a control, and an allowlist adds parsing, compose-parity surface and tests to guard against a user who cannot get there. **One consequence still needed handling, and not with a control:** `main.py` sets `docs_url="/docs" if settings.env != "prod" else None` with `openapi_url` left at default, so on Alpha both `/docs` and `/openapi.json` serve — registering the games router would **publish** the entire API with schemas, converting "nobody knows the paths" into "the paths are indexed". Fixed where it happens: the router registers with **`include_in_schema=False`**. One kwarg, no env setting, no `docker-compose.yml` forwarding, no allowlist. **Residual accepted:** an already-authenticated alpha user who independently guesses an unpublished path could call it; population small and known, paths unadvertised, and the `field_id` cleanup handle covers it. (2) **Both platforms** — *"I have IOS and Android devices, so both build are needed"*; `scripts/install_iphone.sh` and `scripts/install_android.sh` already thread dart-defines and each gains `--dart-define=AMI_GAMES=1`, while `build_testflight.sh`/`build_playstore.sh` are untouched so store binaries carry no games route. (3) **Dark play writes the REAL ledger** — *"real from day 1. we will need history anyway, and we can always clean the data"* — so **no `is_internal` column**; §4.5's `career_events` already carries `field_id` and `entry_id`, making cleanup a field-scoped delete, **which holds only if the scoring pass never writes a row with either null — now an acceptance assertion in slice 3**. (4) **CR133 NO LONGER BLOCKS CR109** — *"if we are building it into the same current app at this phase, we can unblock it"*; §13.1's objection was that the game would ship with nowhere to live, and the hidden route is a temporary home, so CR133 stays deferred and untouched and the game re-homes into the real nav when CR133 ships. **This reverses the "depends on CR133 and must be developed with it" clause above.** **Build scope opened: slices 1, 2 and 3 only** — slice 1 is ungated (it ships the equity curve to the *training* portfolio and has no game surface at all); 3b/3c and beyond are a separate decision after Saiful has played it.
