| CR110 | 2026-07-28 | **Make a mutation run structurally unable to lie — `scripts/mutation_guard.sh` + `failure_patterns.md` P9.** Mutation testing is how this project proves a guard is real, and on 2026-07-28 both halves of that loop produced confident, meaningless results inside a single session. **DEF136:** the matrix ran with `pytest -x`, so pytest stopped at the first failure and never revealed that only one of the two tests was firing — the loop-responsiveness test was **green against a real regression** and was reported as proven. **DEF127:** each mutation was reverted with `git checkout -- <file>` while the fix was still uncommitted; git cannot distinguish a mutation from a fix (both are uncommitted changes to the same file), so it deleted the fix mid-matrix and every number after the first was measured against partially-reverted code. **DEF130:** the identical `git checkout` mistake, **~20 minutes after the operator wrote "never do this" into DEF127's own hand-off.** That third instance is the whole justification for this CR: the rule did not survive one hour as prose, which is CLAUDE.md's *"prompt instructions are not controls"* (CR038) applied to the verification tooling itself — the discipline was living in a hand-off document, precisely where a control must not live. **What ships:** `scripts/mutation_guard.sh <target> <mutate-cmd> <test-cmd>` refuses to proceed if the target is **untracked** (git could not restore it at all — DEF127's `sse.py` kept its mutation because `git checkout` simply errored), refuses if the target has **uncommitted changes** (the DEF127/DEF130 failure), refuses a test command containing **`-x`/`--exitfirst`** (the DEF136 failure), refuses a mutation that **did not actually apply** (a green result there proves nothing), always reverts, and then **verifies the revert by reading `git status`** rather than trusting that the checkout worked. It exits **3** — distinct from any other failure — when the tests **pass** under the mutation, which is the one outcome that means the guard under test is useless. Verified in six states before commit: happy path exit 0; `-x` exit 1; dirty target exit 1; untracked target exit 1; no-op mutation exit 1; tests-pass-under-mutation exit 3; residual diff empty after every run. **Also filed as `failure_patterns.md` P9** with all three instances, per the standing rule that a second occurrence of anything earns an entry **with a guard**. **Known limitation, stated not hidden:** the script is opt-in — nothing forces its use, so it lowers the cost of doing this right rather than making the old way impossible. A hook that refused any `git checkout` of a dirty file would be the stronger control and is deliberately not built here, because it would fight legitimate use. Relates to **DEF136**, **DEF127**, **DEF130**, **CR038** (instructions are not controls), **CR040** (degrade loudly). | done | [CR110_mutation_run_guard/](CR110_mutation_run_guard/) | AT:R65 |

Verify both at 1.0 and 1.15 text scale in AR before calling it done. `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — the two new header strings plus any chip label touched. ONLY narrows where they can invest; NEVER puts something off the table entirely"* — and each chip carries its own direction rather than relying on a header: `ONLY halal / Sharia-compliant`, `ONLY ESG-leaning`, `ONLY liquid names (no microcaps)`, `ONLY long positions (no shorting)`, `NEVER tobacco, alcohol or gambling`, `NEVER fossil fuels`, `No hard rules`. **Per-chip prefixes rather than the grouped ONLY/NEVER headers the spec proposed:** the chip list is a flat array the client renders as tappable pills, so a header row would either be a tappable non-answer or a client-side change — and the whole point of doing this server-side was that it reaches already-installed builds. | CR117 | 2026-07-29 | **The app's "hexagons" are octagons — add a real hexagon clipper, migrate the controls that should be hexagonal, and stop the class name lying.** Saiful, bug report `589e7607` (Platinum Anchor, `0.1.0+57`), on the ticker period toggle: *"the buttons are octagonal, not hexagonal."* **Correct, and the code already admits it.** [`hex_clipper.dart:11-14`](../../../mobile/lib/theme/hex_clipper.dart#L11-L14) declares `class FlatTopHexagonClipper` whose own docstring reads *"Cut-corner octagon — what the design system spec calls a 'hex clip-path'"*, and `getClip` emits an **8-point path**: it cuts all four corners of the rect, producing two angled ends **plus** angled top and bottom. A flat-top hexagon has six sides — angled ends, flat top and bottom — which is exactly what the sibling `FlatTopRegularHexagon` (:47) draws for agent avatars and the honeycomb. **So the app ships two different shapes under one name**, and every "hex" *control* is an octagon: `HexButton`, `HexChip`, `GlassPanel` accents, `ticker_chart.dart:185`'s period toggle, and the BOARD segment of the Room toggle. Only the avatars and honeycomb are genuinely hexagonal. On a small chip the difference is subliminal; on the wide, saturated, selected period pill in the screenshot it is unmistakable, which is why this surfaced on the toggle first. **This reframes DEF146 and is the reason it cannot ship without this CR.** The AT:Designer's toggle (`df515c35`) is a **true hexagon** — angled cuts on the outer edges only, flat top and bottom, straight internal divider. That shape is **not producible** by `FlatTopHexagonClipper` at any `cornerCut`, so DEF146's fix was mis-scoped as "apply the same clipper to both halves"; it needs the new path this CR builds. **RULED (Saiful, 2026-07-29 0900 check-in): "Add a real hexagon clipper, migrate controls to it."** Rejected: rename-only (leaves DEF146 unbuildable) and a two-shape rule with no principle for choosing. **Scope:** (1) add a true flat-top hexagon path for *rect-proportioned* controls — note this is **not** `FlatTopRegularHexagon`, which is locked to a 2:√3 bounding box and will not stretch to a button's aspect ratio without distorting the angle; the new clipper takes a corner inset and cuts only the left and right edges. (2) Migrate the controls that should read as hexagonal, **starting with the DEF146 toggle**, which is the one with a signed-off design. (3) **Rename `FlatTopHexagonClipper` to what it is** (`CutCornerOctagonClipper` or similar) — the name has misled every reader since it was written, including the CR106 spec work that reasoned about "hex geometry" on controls that have none. **Deliberately open, to be decided during the work rather than guessed here:** which of the remaining controls become true hexagons and which stay octagons. Do **not** sweep them all — the octagon has shipped for months and reads as intentional; migrate on evidence (a design, or a report like this one), not on tidiness. Note **CR113** removes the shape from large CTAs entirely, so those are out of scope here, and **CR108** edits `TrackHexButton`, which already uses the true-hexagon clipper and must not be caught in the migration. Update `ami_hex_in_flutter.md` alongside CR113's rule so the two shapes and their uses are documented in one place. Relates to **DEF146** (blocked on this), **CR113** (removes octagons from CTAs), **CR106 §4.0** (reasoned about "hex" controls that are octagons), **CR108** (adjacent, must not be swept).  **DELIVERED (AT:R65, 2026-07-29) — the mechanical half, in full; the open design question left open as the CR directed.** Built ahead of CR120 rather than beside it, because CR120's segmented tabs are specified as *"hex-clipped, `cornerCut: 8`, matching `ticker_chart.dart:185`"* — one of the twelve call sites this CR renames. Laning them in parallel would have had CR120 build its tabs in the octagon this CR exists to stop, on an identifier being renamed underneath it. **(1) The true hexagon: `FlatTopHexagonBarClipper`** — angled ends, flat top and bottom, six sides, free `endInset` so it holds its angle at any aspect ratio. Confirmed by measurement that neither existing class could do the job: `CutCornerOctagonClipper` cuts the top and bottom at every `cornerCut`, and `FlatTopRegularHexagon`'s diagonals start at a fixed `w * 0.25`, so on a 200×40 bar it flattens into a near-triangle — a point 40pt in from the end is inside the new bar's flat top and outside the regular hexagon's, which is pinned as a test. **(2) The rename: 12 sites across 9 files**, `FlatTopHexagonClipper` → `CutCornerOctagonClipper`. **The new class deliberately did NOT inherit the vacated name**, which is the one judgement call here: it is what the name always claimed, but had it taken it, any unmigrated call site — or one written in a lane in flight, which is precisely the situation CR120 creates — would keep compiling and *silently change shape*. Because `FlatTopHexagonClipper` now names nothing, a stale reference is a **compile error instead of a wrong shape**: CLAUDE.md's degrade-loudly rule applied to a rename. **(3) DEF146 migrated and thereby closed** (see its row). **The guard counts sides**, which is the property the name makes a claim about and the one nothing checked: `getBounds` is identical for all three clippers, which is exactly why an octagon shipped under a hexagon's name for months. The test walks the path, recovers its vertices from direction changes, and asserts 8 / 6 / 6. *(Its first version reported 7 and 5 — the walk skipped the corner sitting on the path's seam. Fixed to be cyclic; noted because a shape guard that is quietly one side short is worse than none.)* Plus a **name guard** that fails if the old identifier is reintroduced as a compatibility alias, matching it in **code position only** so the docstring that explains the rename does not trip it — with its own vacuity check that the regex can still see a violation. **Two mutations independently RED:** give the hexagon bar cut top and bottom (i.e. make it an octagon again); reintroduce `typedef FlatTopHexagonClipper = CutCornerOctagonClipper` and point a call site at it. Rejected: top-N with a "show all" expander (avoids nested scrolling but hides allocations behind a tap — and the whole point of the card is that the user can see their concentration at a glance), and deferring into the `9d51ce11` design work (**CR119**), which covers the same growing-lists problem for watchlist/holdings/trades but at a slower cadence than this one-card fix needs. **Implementation note, because this is the part that goes wrong:** the card lives inside `portfolio_screen.dart`'s top-level `ListView` (`:137`), so an inner scrollable needs a bounded height and its own `ScrollController` — an unbounded nested `ListView` inside a `ListView` throws, and a `shrinkWrap` one silently re-expands to full content height, which would look fixed in a 4-sector test and regress the moment someone diversifies. Test with a synthetic 13-row allocation, not the reporter's 4. Also give the capped list a visible affordance that it scrolls (a fade or partial row at the cut) — a list that is clipped with no cue reads as a rendering bug, which is how this same pattern produced clipped-CTA reports under **DEF075**. **BUILT 2026-07-29 (AT:R65).** Mine to build rather than the CR120 lane's: this was folded in as that lane's **acceptance 11** by amendment `ba0aa979`, which landed *after* the worker branched at `2f49e350`, and `claude -p` is one-shot — so the lane never saw the requirement. Verified absent by grep before building, and **not a finding against the builder**. **Shape:** the legend is a **fixed**-height viewport, not a maximum, so the card's footprint is constant whatever the allocation; rows carry a fixed **22pt** extent so *"does this scroll"* is arithmetic rather than text measurement, which is the only reason the boundary is testable at all. **One deliberate deviation from this row, stated rather than quietly taken:** it asks for "approximately the donut's height" (72pt) and the build uses **99pt (4.5 rows)**. At 3.5 rows the number would be 77 and much closer, but it would make **the reporter's own four-sector portfolio start scrolling** — a present regression for the person who filed a forward-looking request. 4.5 rows leaves every typical allocation static and still bounds the card; the boundary is 5+ sectors. **The half-row at the cut is the affordance**, with a `ShaderMask` bottom fade over it, and **both appear only when something is actually hidden** — a fade with nothing behind it is a lie, and this row is explicit that a list clipped with no cue reads as a rendering bug (the **DEF075** shape). **Both nested-scrollable traps this row names are handled:** the list has its **own `ScrollController`** (without one it attaches to the inherited `PrimaryScrollController` and drives the outer view instead of itself) and uses **`NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` when the content fits**, so a legend with nothing to scroll cannot swallow a drag meant for the screen. **Guard: 5 tests, measured against the 13-sector fixture this row demands, not the reporter's four** — and read off the render tree with `getSize` rather than asserting a widget exists, because *"it is capped"* is a claim about **height**, and a `shrinkWrap` list would satisfy a widget-existence check while silently re-expanding to full content height. The footprint test carries its own non-vacuity check (fade absent at 4, present at 13) so *"the height did not change"* cannot pass on two identical renders, and one test exists purely to prove **nothing is lost behind the cap**: scroll to the tail and the 12th sector really is there while the first has really gone. **Mutations measured:** removing the fixed height and adding `shrinkWrap: true` → **3 RED**; dropping the fade → **2 RED**; making the list always scrollable → **1 RED**. **Found while writing the tests:** pumping the same widget types twice reuses the element tree, so Riverpod served the *previous* allocation for a frame and the 4-sector case was silently asserting against 13-sector state — it presented as a genuine failure; the harness now tears the tree down between pumps. Mobile 284 green at commit (299 after the same day's DEF151/DEF139/DEF156 pass), `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos` exit 0. **CR116 was dropped** (superseded by CR120's tabs), so the "sequence them in one pass" note below is moot. Note **CR116** reorders this screen's sections in the same file; sequence them in one pass. Relates to **CR119** (the broader redesign this anticipates), **CR116** (same file, same lane), **DEF075** (clipped-content-without-affordance precedent). **FOLDED INTO [CR120](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/CR120.md) (Saiful, 2026-07-29), and dispatched into that lane as Amendment 1 while it was already running.** The Architect had recommended *holding* this until CR120 integrated; Saiful overruled, and the overrule is the better call — **CR120 moves this donut into the Positions tab**, so the lane worker is the one holding its new home, and a follow-up would have been specified against a layout that no longer exists. Delivered as CR120 **acceptance 11**: constant card height at 4 sectors and at 13, legend scrolling within its own bounds, visible affordance at the cut. This row's implementation note went across **verbatim**, because that note is the whole value of the item — an unbounded nested `ListView` throws and a `shrinkWrap` one *silently re-expands to full content height*, which looks correct in a 4-sector fixture and regresses the moment someone diversifies — with one correction: **the container is no longer the top-level `ListView` at `:137`** that the note was written against, so the nesting must be re-read before the height is bounded. **Caveat recorded honestly:** `claude -p` is one-shot, so if the worker had already read its assign file the amendment is invisible to it; the Architect verifies acceptance 11 at integration and builds it there if absent. **CR116, which this row said to sequence in the same pass, was dropped** — CR120 supersedes it. | done | — | AT:R65 |
| CR119 | 2026-07-29 | **Portfolio screen redesign — watchlist, holdings and trades all grow without bound; commission AT:Design.** Saiful, bug report `9d51ce11` (Platinum Anchor, `0.1.0+57`): *"in Portfolio, the watchlist, holding and trades will all increase in numbers. we need a better way to view them. we need a AT:Design to work on this."* Filed as a **design commission**, not an implementation CR — the instruction names the owner, so no solution is proposed here and none should be inferred from this row. **The structural problem, stated so the designer has the constraints rather than the symptom.** [`portfolio_screen.dart:137-160`](../../../mobile/lib/screens/sim/portfolio_screen.dart#L137-L160) is a single top-level `ListView` whose children are laid out in full: `_ValueCard` → `_SectorAllocationSection` → `_WatchlistSection` → the holdings block (one `_HoldingCard` per position) → the trades block. **Three of those five are unbounded**, and every one of them grows through exactly the behaviour the product is trying to teach — watch more tickers, hold more positions, trade more often. A user the app has succeeded with is a user whose portfolio screen is unusable. Today's reporter sits at 89.3% cash with 4 sector rows and a short list, so nothing is broken yet; this is a scaling ceiling, filed before it is hit. **Interactions the design has to absorb, all decided today and all in this file:** **CR116** moves holdings above the watchlist, **CR118** caps and scrolls the sector legend, and CR116's row flags that the holdings block is a conditional (`if (p.holdings.isEmpty)` renders `_NewTraderHint`), so the empty state is a distinct layout, not a degenerate case of the populated one. A redesign that ignores the empty state will regress the new-trader experience DEF060 exists to protect. Also live in this screen: `_watchlistKey`, a `GlobalKey` used as a scroll/coach-mark target, which any restructure must keep attached. **Open questions for the design, not for this row:** whether the three lists become tabs, sections with independent scroll, or separate screens; what the summary state of a collapsed list shows (count? top holding? total value?); and whether trades — the least-referenced and fastest-growing of the three — belongs on this screen at all rather than behind the Journal, which is already the durable record surface. **Sequencing:** CR116 and CR118 are small, ruled and land first; they are not blocked on this and should not wait for it. This CR stays `proposed` until AT:Design delivers, at which point it gets a spec folder and a normal build lane. Precedent for the handoff: **DEF146**, where the Designer's output arrived as a bug-report attachment and became the normative source for the fix. **CLOSED (Saiful, 2026-07-29): the commission was delivered same-day as [CR120](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/CR120.md).** AT:Design built and measured all four candidate structures on identical data in a live prototype — today's screen, segmented tabs, a bounded dashboard and collapsible sections — read scroll extents out of the DOM at 390×844 rather than estimating, and Saiful chose **segmented tabs** (heavy profile: 25.4 screens today → 2.9–4.2 across three tabs, worst reachable 4.2). CR120 also answered two of the three open questions this row posed: **trades stay on this screen** — the design found the premise *"users can still check trades in the Journal"* is **half false**, since Floor Pass gets 30-day journal retention while `sim_trades` has none, so for a free user the Portfolio is the **durable** record and the Journal the lossy one; and the collapsed-summary question dissolved, since a tab shows its **count** in the label, which is what tells a user the other two are not empty. This row closes as **done** because its deliverable was a design, and the design exists; the implementation is tracked as CR120. | done | [CR120_portfolio_list_structure/](CR120_portfolio_list_structure/) | AT:R65 |
| CR120 | 2026-07-29 | **Portfolio: structure for three growing lists, and a cap on trade history.** Saiful: *"The portfolio screen has watchlist, holdings and trade history. They will all grow. We need a better way than simple scrolling one after another. We also need to limit the trades to either a number of items… or of a period… Users can still check trades in the Journal instead."* **Measured, from the DOM of a built prototype at 390×844, not estimated:** `portfolio_screen.dart:137` is a `ListView(children:)` — **not `.builder`** — so every row is constructed on every rebuild, and since `TradeRow`/`_WatchlistRow` are `ConsumerWidget`s under a `ref.watch(simNotifierProvider)`, a price tick rebuilds all of them: **3.6 screens / 31 rows** at a modest account, **8.9 / 84** at six months, **25.4 / 252** at heavy use. Growth is linear and unbounded because nothing is capped server-side either — `sim_engine.py:447 list_trades` selects every trade the user has ever made, `opened_at DESC`, no `limit`, no `offset`. **Three structural findings shaped the fix.** (1) **Open and closed trades are interleaved by open date** — there is no status split in the render path (`:170`), so a live position opened in April sits below forty closed trades from May; **open trades are money at risk, not history, and are never capped in any option**. (2) **The watchlist is not user-curated — it auto-grows**: `sim.py:302` silently adds every traded ticker and `watchlist_store.add` has no cap, so the same ticker can appear in all three sections without the user ever touching it. (3) The sector donut renders above the watchlist today and reads as unrelated to anything; it belongs inside Holdings. **The premise needed correcting, and the correction is binding.** *"Users can still check trades in the Journal"* is **half true**: every trade does write a journal entry carrying the full trade JSON (`sim.py:314`, `:393`, `:446`) and the Journal already ships a TRADE filter chip plus search — **but Floor Pass gets 30-day retention** (`journal_store.py:42-47`, `FLOOR_PASS_RETENTION_DAYS = 30`) while `sim_trades` has none. For a free user the relationship is **inverted — the Portfolio is the durable record and the Journal is the lossy one** — so a fetch-limit cap pointing at the Journal would silently delete their own trade history from every surface (CR040, degrade loudly, with the user's data as the thing lost). **That one line is the entire plan-dependent surface of the screen** — verified, not assumed: not a single `plan` reference in `sim.py` or `watchlist.py`, and no plan-gated limit anywhere in the sim path (`credit_service`/`reputation_service` hold the only plan gates and neither touches the Portfolio), so Floor Pass vs Trader is one caveat appearing or not, beneath the action it qualifies — deliberate placement, since a user does not need to know about Journal retention until they are about to rely on the Journal, but it does make the difference invisible from the landing tab. **THE CLIENT MUST NOT BRANCH ON PLAN — it branches on `retention_days`.** Saiful, seeing the toggle: *"So a slightly different UI depending on plan."* Yes, but not implemented as one, and the distinction is load-bearing: the Journal list response already carries `retention_days`, the client already parses it (`journal.dart:141` → `JournalState.retentionDays`), and **the Journal screen already renders an amber notice from it** (`journal_screen.dart:113-120`) — so CR120 is **extending a shipped disclosure to the screen that links to it**, not inventing a pattern (reinventing it would be DEF098's two-renderer class on a monetisation-adjacent string), and the UI branches on *"is there a retention window?"* — an integer, or `null` for unlimited, computed server-side. No plan state to sync, no wrong-branch risk from a stale client idea of the plan, and a policy change reaches users without a release. **Never hardcode 30 in the app.** **Fail-safe:** `retention_days` today only arrives on the journal list response, which the Portfolio never calls, so if it is unknown the Portfolio shows the caveat **without a number** and never the reassuring branch — a spurious warning is recoverable, a missing one is the thing the section exists to prevent (CR040); **B3** (`journal_retention_days` on the sim portfolio/trades response) removes the guess. **NOTHING IS DELETED — AND THE SHIPPED STRING SAYS OTHERWISE.** Writing the honest version exposed a defect in the one already live: `journalRetentionWarning` reads *"Floor Pass: last {days} days only. Upgrade to keep everything."* but **retention is a read-time filter** (`journal_store.py:134-136` appends `where created_at >= cutoff` to the select; the only `delete(JournalEntryRow)` in the store is a test-only `clear()`), so an entry outside the window is hidden, not destroyed, and reappears on upgrade — and for sim trades it is doubly wrong, since `sim_trades` has no retention at all. *"Upgrade to **keep** everything"* asserts a data loss that is not happening in order to drive a purchase, in shipped user-facing copy on a paid-conversion surface: CR038/DEF059's confident-wrongness family. Fix is one verb (*keep* → *see*) plus a clause saying nothing is lost; filed as defect #7 with `retranslate:[ar,ms]`, **not edited unilaterally** because it sits on a conversion surface. CR120's own line says what is true: *"Your Journal shows the last 30 days — 47 of these 57 are older. Nothing is deleted; they stay here."* Hence: the cap is a **view default with an in-place escape hatch, never a fetch limit** (`SHOW ALL 57` reads the Portfolio's own durable data), and the Journal pointer is **plan-aware** — *"Journal keeps 30 days on Floor Pass — 47 of these 57 are older. They stay here."* **The cap, decided by Saiful: last 25, with the span they cover stated** (`LAST 25 CLOSED · 17 MAY – 28 JUL`) — the period is **described, never used to filter**, because a pure period filter shows an empty history to a user who took a break and shows all 200 to a day-trader who did not, while a combination must choose union (unbounded) or intersection (empty). Above it sits a summary computed over **all** closed trades, not the visible 25 (a hit rate over an arbitrary display window is a wrong number wearing the authority of a statistic): win/loss bar, `WON 41 · LOST 16 · 72% · NET +$39,330`. **Four structures built and measured on identical data before the call** — landing screens at modest / six-month / heavy, plus the worst state a user can reach: **today 3.6 / 8.9 / 25.4** (no other state exists); **bounded dashboard 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.2** (3.2, bounded by construction); **segmented tabs 1.0 / 1.4 / 2.3** as first built, before open trades moved to the landing tab; **collapsible sections 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.4** (**9.7 with everything expanded** — a number the user can undo with two taps). I recommended the bounded dashboard and flagged the tab risk — a horizontal switcher nested inside the bottom-nav tab the user is already in, with **no tab pattern anywhere in the app** outside `alpaca_connect_screen.dart`. Saiful chose tabs; the mitigations are below. **STRUCTURE DECIDED 2026-07-29 — segmented tabs.** Saiful chose tabs after reviewing all four in the prototype. Three hex-clipped segments (`cornerCut: 8`, matching `ticker_chart.dart:185` and CR106's BOARD|TRANSCRIPT toggle) under a pinned compact value card; fill flip only, no sliding indicator and **no swipe-between-tabs** (the DS rules out motion on text, and a horizontal swipe inside a bottom-nav tab fights the OS back gesture). **POSITIONS carries holdings AND open trades, so HISTORY is closed trades only and its count says `195`, not `200`** — this is the one thing the structure could get wrong, since an open trade is money at risk with a stop that can fire and a tab the user does not land on makes it invisible; it also dissolves the interleave defect, because no list contains both any more. The sector donut moves inside Positions where it describes the list beneath it. **Tab state is `TabController` state, never a persisted preference.** Saiful asked whether the Portfolio should land on Positions or resume the last tab; the answer is *both, at different scopes*, and the shipped shell already gives all three for free — `home_shell.dart:42` hosts the nav destinations in an **`IndexedStack`**, so `PortfolioScreen`'s State lives for the whole app session: a push-and-pop keeps the tab, a bottom-nav round trip keeps the tab, and a relaunch lands on Positions. **Doing nothing is the whole implementation** — no prefs key, no stale-preference migration, none of CR106's T-MODESIDE trap surface. Persisting across launches is rejected for the same reason open trades moved onto the landing tab: a user whose last visit ended on History would open the app the next day with an armed stop behind a tab they cannot see, and since the pinned value card shows total value, P&L and cash on every tab regardless, the *only* thing landing on History costs is sight of the live positions. A staleness rule ("reset if resumed after N minutes") is also rejected — a tab that sometimes remembers and sometimes does not is worse than either rule applied consistently. **The Positions tab carries a live pip when an open trade exists**, since its count is holdings and therefore under-reports its own contents; a second number would conflate two different things and tab labels have no width to spare, so it is a 6pt flat-top hex in family cyan — **not amber, because an open position is a state, not a warning** — that turns `textHigh` when the tab is active and is absent when there are none. **A list over 12 items gets search + sort inside its own tab** (what a full viewport per list buys, and what the rejected dashboard could not offer without a navigation), with per-list defaults rather than one generic sort: holdings by value, watchlist A–Z (a watchlist is scanned to *find* a name, and movers-first moves the name every day), closed newest. **Measured per tab** — Positions 1.1 / 1.7 / 2.9, Watchlist 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.2, History 2.8 / 3.7 / 3.7 screens across modest / six-month / heavy: **History stops growing at six months**, which is the 25-cap doing its job, while **Watchlist is the one unbounded tab** and is unbounded for a reason nobody chose (the auto-add above) — search and sort make 40 rows navigable, not 200, so that needs its own conversation if the auto-add stays. The summary strip is captioned `ACROSS ALL 195 CLOSED` so it cannot be read as a statistic about the visible 25. Tab labels are the tightest strings on the screen (~117pt each); `POSITIONS 12` fits at 1.0 and 1.15 in EN, and **AR/MS need re-checking once translated** — a `FittedBox` shrinking a tab label is CR108 over again. Rejected: the bounded dashboard (flattest at 3.2 and nothing behind a mode, but no list ever gets a full viewport) and collapsible sections (2.4 screens is a state the user can undo with two taps → 9.7); both kept live in the prototype so the comparison stays auditable. **RTL verification caught a live instance of CR106's T-BIDI trap**: `+$5,423.69 (+5.33%)` reordered to `(5.33%+` — every run mixing sign, digits and parens is now bidi-isolated (the layout mirrors, the numbers do not). **Phase 1 needs nothing from the backend** — structure + section split + the 25-cap + the summary + the plan-aware pointer are all view concerns over data already fetched, plus `ListView.builder`; pagination (`limit`/`offset`/`total` on `GET /v1/sim/trades`, and honouring the existing unused `status=` filter) is Phase 3, wanted by the pushed all-trades route which today fetches the whole ledger to render a 25-row tab. **Seven defects spotted, flagged to the Architect to mint, not filed here:** open trades buried in history; the eager `ListView(children:)` itself; the trade→journal write wrapped in `except Exception: pass` (`sim.py:328` and two more — silent, and much more expensive once the Portfolio points at the Journal); the Journal list endpoint at `limit=100` with no pagination despite returning `total`; the undisclosed auto-growing watchlist; `_WatchlistRow` setting the price at 24px `statMid` against a 12px ticker, so the price shouts and the identity whispers; and **`journalRetentionWarning` claiming a data loss that does not happen** (see above — one verb, but on a paid-conversion surface). `retranslate:[ar,ms]` — 16 proposed ARB ids in the spec. | CR121 | 2026-07-29 | **Client version gate: a server-driven minimum build, with a message per raise.** Saiful: *"research how I can force an update on the app on the users phone"* → *"Create a CR for the gate. Make it such that we can send a message as well to the user when we ask them to update. Message will be added for each time we move the bar."* **Measured: no gate exists at any layer** — zero hits for `min_version`/`force_update`/`upgrade_required` across `backend/app/**/*.py` and `mobile/lib/**/*.dart`. But the plumbing is already half-built and terminates in a DB column instead of a decision: the client computes its own version (`device_user.dart:46` → `"0.1.0+57"`), ships it on bootstrap (`api_client.dart:980-992` → `schemas/auth.py:65` → `api/auth.py:119`), and the server stores it (`models.py:120,189`) — it just never acts on it. **The honest ceiling:** iOS has **no** force-update API, so "force" = the app refuses to run below the floor and hands the user a one-tap route to the store. That is the only mechanism working on both platforms and every channel we use (TestFlight, Play internal/closed, App Store, cable). **Design:** the floor is *append-only, one row per raise* (`client_release_floors`), not a mutable setting — each raise carries its own `headline`/`body_en`/`body_ar`/`body_ms`, active floor = highest `min_build`, and `active=false` retracts a bad raise without losing the history. Unauthenticated `GET /v1/client/release-floor` (sibling of `/v1/health`, `main.py:209` — must answer *before* a session exists, since a blocked client may be too old to authenticate) returns a server-decided `action: block|nag|ok` plus locale-resolved copy, so policy changes without a client release; `426 Upgrade Required` enforces server-side off a new `X-App-Version` header added at the single existing choke point (`api_client.dart:52-64`), with `/v1/health`, the floor endpoint itself and the feedback POST exempt so a stuck user can still report it. Mobile catches the 426 in a `_VersionGateInterceptor` modelled on DEF073's `_ServerErrorInterceptor` (`api_client.dart:72-89`), checks on launch **and** on foreground-resume, and raises a non-dismissible screen. Write side is `POST /v1/admin/release-floor` behind the existing `ADMIN_SECRET` bearer (`api/admin.py:54-63`) — a raise is one API call, no deploy, no container recreate, which is why it's a table and not an env var. **Floor is one integer, not a per-platform pair:** `pubspec.yaml` carries a single `version: <semver>+<build>` that `build_testflight.sh:81-99` bumps and `publish_playstore.sh --no-bump` reuses, so comparison is integer `>=` on the build number, no semver parsing. **Deliberate exception to degrade-loudly:** the gate **fails open** — a fail-closed gate turns any melehost outage into a simultaneous brick of every installed client, strictly worse than briefly serving a stale build; the failure is logged and surfaced in the admin config check, never swallowed. **Sequencing constraint:** a gate only binds builds that already contain it, so `0.1.0+57` and everything before is permanently ungateable — worth landing before the next TestFlight round so `+58` is the first gateable build. **Operational footgun guarded:** the admin write path refuses a `min_build` above the highest build ever observed in `user_devices.last_app_version` without an explicit force flag, because raising the floor above what TestFlight has approved bricks every iOS tester with nowhere to go. iOS store deep link needs a numeric App Store ID we do not have (falls back to the TestFlight join link; same provisioning dependency as DEF100/CR084), and the bundle IDs differ per platform (`ai.agenticmarketintel.amiTrade` vs `ai.agenticmarketintel.ami_trade`) so nothing may derive a store URL from one value. ~5 new ARB keys need ar/ms; the per-raise message itself is operational copy with EN fallback, not shipped content. **Out of scope:** Play In-App Updates immediate flow (Android-only polish on a tap this already covers; `inAppUpdatePriority` is Publishing-API-only and unsupported on internal app sharing), Shorebird OTA (Dart-only, own CR), and bricking the legacy base by refusing `/v1/auth/device` (documented emergency lever, not built). Coordinate with the on-prem→Supabase swap point noted in `dependencies.py` so the `exp`/version scheme survives that migration. mobile+api domain; before next promotion. Under CR123. **BUILT 2026-08-07 (AT:R66), not yet promoted.** Backend: `_scaffold_token`/`parse_scaffold_token` in `auth_service.py` now emit/verify `scaffold:<hex>:<exp>:<ver>:<sig>` (HMAC over all three fields, so `exp`/`ver` can't be rewritten offline); the pre-CR125 3-part signed format is rejected outright everywhere (CR040 degrade-loudly), not silently downgraded. `users.token_version` (Alembic `2851822570ac`, single head) is the revocation counter; `api/dependencies.py::get_current_user`/`get_current_user_optional` are the one enforcement point that checks it against the DB (kept out of the parse function on purpose — the module docstring's Supabase-JWT swap point stays a one-function change). `DELETE /v1/auth/session` bumps it, so sign-out now actually revokes every outstanding token, not just the local copy — closed a real gap where `/v1/auth/anon` would otherwise happily re-mint a fresh valid token for a bearer that had just been signed out (`anon_session` now runs its bearer check through `get_current_user_optional`, which enforces `exp`+`ver`). this **deliberately inverts CR101-BE2's acceptance 4** (where `None` meant off precisely so nobody was silently constrained) and the new acceptance is its mirror — prove every user's limits DO change, to the right values for their score; **"off" stays expressible** per CR101's amendment, needing no new representation because each of the seven has a natural off value that is already legal (cooldown `0`, percentages `100`, counts set high) and L3's loud-disclosure path already covers choosing it; | CR131 | 2026-07-30 | **BACKEND BUILT 2026-08-07 (AT:R66); the surfacing UI is a separate slice.** **Instrument the Day Trader preset so it teaches instead of just permitting** — CR129 adds a preset that sets every user risk limit permissive, on Saiful's reasoning that *"if we do not let them fail in a safe environment, they will fail with real money."* Correct, and consistent with CR101's L3 — but **a preset that only removes limits is a faster way to lose with nothing learned**, and a user who switches it on, loses steadily and draws no conclusion has had exactly the real-money experience this app exists to replace. **Shipped:** `backend/app/services/day_trader_outcomes.py` + a read-only ownership-guarded endpoint on the portfolio router. Cohort boundary is the **earliest** `MANDATE_EDIT` journal entry whose summary marks the preset applied (`mandate.py:154` writes it); no such entry ⇒ not in the cohort and nothing is computed. Metrics: trade frequency, **turnover** (so the comparison is like-for-like with Barber–Odean rather than rhetorical), realised P&L, win rate, average win/loss, average hold. Turnover is measured against the fixed sim starting capital rather than a time-weighted average portfolio value — an explicit approximation of the Barber–Odean definition, chosen because every sim portfolio starts at the same known figure and it therefore needs no new table; **recorded as an approximation in the code, not passed off as the literal metric**. **The honesty rules are the acceptance, and both are mutation-proven:** a thin sample (< 10 trades OR < 7 days on **either** side of the boundary) returns a refusal carrying **no figure at all** — not a zero, not an extrapolation — and forcing `_meets_threshold` to `True` turns 2 tests red; dropping the preset-marker check turns 7 red. It does not moralise (no grade, no warning, no copy telling the user they are doing badly) and it does not special-case a losing user — a winning user gets the same shape, beside the plain fact that <1% sustain it and that a short winning window is Barber & Odean's own proposed mechanism for the overconfidence driving excess trading. Baselines carry their provenance (US 1991–1996 / Taiwan 1992–2006 retail equity) so nothing implies they describe this user's market, and reuse the figures verified for CR132's lessons 366–370 rather than re-deriving them. **DEF166 checked before relying on `realised_pnl`** (it concerned clamped closes stamping the full quantity): `status != "open"` is the correct trustworthiness filter and also excludes SELL-side rows without a side check. **No migration and no `Settings` field** — deliberate, both to keep it off the shared Alembic head another lane was moving and because everything needed already exists in `journal_entries` + `sim_trades`. **Still owed:** the mobile surface, and CR132's **lesson 6** ("running the experiment on yourself"), which links to this. **AUDIT: AWAITING_FIXES r1 — 1 MAJOR, 2 MINOR — and the MAJOR was the seam I flagged and then declined to fix.** I named the cohort-marker coupling as this CR's weakest point and argued a shared constant was the better fix but that CR129 owned the file. A first audit pass agreed with me and returned COMPLETE; **a second pass ran the adversarial test instead of deferring, and it changed the answer.** Rewording `mandate.py`'s summary from "…preset applied — …" to "…preset now active — …" (still containing "Day Trader preset", the only thing CR129's own adjacent test checks) left the **entire 2589-test suite green** while `compute_day_trader_outcomes()` silently returned `not_in_cohort` for a user who had just switched — indistinguishable from "nobody has tried the preset". Zero existing tests caught it, because every CR131 test drove the marker through a helper built *from the constant itself*, so none could ever see real drift. Live risk, not hypothetical: an active `coder.api-CR129-BE` worktree is editing that copy right now. **Fixed structurally:** `DAY_TRADER_JOURNAL_MARKER` + `DAY_TRADER_JOURNAL_SUMMARY` now live once, in `day_trader_preset.py` (the preset is what both sides are describing); `mandate.py` imports the summary and `day_trader_outcomes.py` re-exports the marker, so **no literal copy survives anywhere** and there is nothing left to drift. Re-running the auditor's exact exploit now leaves detection working, because both sides move together. The auditor's `test_cr131_cohort_marker_coupling_pin.py` is kept and registered in DEF141's `MIGRATED_PINS`. **MINOR (fixed):** this row said the elapsed-days floor was **14**; the shipped code says **7.0**. I wrote 14 from my own build brief and never checked it against the implementation — a docs-vs-code mismatch of exactly the kind this register exists to prevent. **MINOR (accepted):** `sent`-style counters mean a call was made, not delivery confirmed. **The thin-sample rule survived 13 adversarial probes** — boundary counts, the real 7.0-day floor at 6d23h45m, 200-vs-1 lopsided windows, zero trades on either side, ~80 trades crammed into 9 hours — every refusal a hard `{status, message}` with **zero numeric leaves** on a recursive walk, not even a digit in the message. | CR132 | 2026-07-30 | **LESSONS 1–5 BUILT 2026-08-07 (AT:R66); lesson 6 still blocked on CR131.** **A Day Trader lesson track, grounded in the behavioural-finance research** — Saiful: *"I need the education material to have the research you just did. Content: 366 the Taiwan numbers without editorial; 367 the 11.4% vs 18.5% turnover finding; 368 overconfidence + the disposition effect; 369 the tilt spiral with the cortisol/testosterone literature; 370 what skill persistence actually looks like. **Sourcing was verified against primary sources, and the verification did real work — three figures were rejected rather than written:** a search-sourced Taiwan survival curve of "80% quit within 2 years, 13% by 3, 7% by 5" that appears nowhere in the primary PDF (the paper's Kaplan-Meier figures are **44%/24%/15%** at 1/2/3 years, and those are what shipped); Coates & Herbert's widely-quoted "74% testosterone rise on a winning streak", which is discussion in the PNAS paper and not a reported result; and Locke & Mann's disposition-effect cost figure, dropped because their 2000 working paper and 2005 JFE paper give irreconcilable summaries. **AUDIT ROUND 1 = AWAITING_FIXES, 1 BLOCKER, and it caught an error I had personally cleared.** 368's "men traded 45% more and earned risk-adjusted net returns 1.4 points lower / single men 67% more and 2.3 points lower" — I flagged it as suspicious, "verified" it, and passed it. What I actually checked was a **search-engine summary of the SSRN working-paper abstract**; the lesson cites the **published QJE 116(1), 2001**. The auditor fetched that PDF and read §III.A/§III.B/Table IV directly: **`2.3` appears nowhere in the cited paper**, `1.4` is real but is the *singles* figure (footnote 21's three-factor model, per a second independent pass) not the full-sample one, and — worse than the magnitude — the paper states raw net-return differences between men and women are **not statistically significant** (16.3% vs 16.9%, reversed in sign), so "men earned lower returns" was wrong in *direction*. Quiz 1 graded the wrong pairing as correct. **Round 2 fix:** the lesson now uses the cited version's own trading-cost measure end to end — 2.65pp/yr men vs 1.72 women → a **0.93pp** gap, widening to **1.44pp** among singles — so both halves come from one measure and both are quotable from the paper's own abstract. Keeping `1.4` was rejected deliberately: there is no published three-factor singles breakdown, so it would have forced mixing measures across one sentence, which is the error that caused the bug. Body, hypothesis sentence and Quiz 1 updated together. **Guard:** 368's `sources:` now carries an explicit do-not-use note naming the 1.4/2.3 pair as the superseded working-paper abstract's, because the second audit pass measured **WebSearch echoing that wrong pairing verbatim across two independent queries with no citation** — a search engine repeating a figure is not corroboration, it is the same uncited claim twice, and no test can catch that class. **MINOR also fixed:** 369 said institutions "showed no such pattern" on the break-even effect; proprietary futures firms **do** show it, they just don't move volatility/liquidity the way individuals do — the difference is market impact, not immunity. **23 of 24 numeric claims CONFIRMED** against primary sources by the auditor, several to the exact digit. Original review note retained: 368's figures  "men traded 45% more and earned risk-adjusted net returns 1.4 points lower / single men 67% more and 2.3 points lower" looked transposed against the QJE abstract's 2.65-vs-1.72 framing, but those are two different quantities in the same paper (reduction-from-trading vs the risk-adjusted net-return gap) and the working-paper abstract states 1.4 / 2.3 verbatim. 366 is careful to separate the **18.6% one-year** bar (luck included) from the **<1% persistence** bar (ranked, re-tested out of sample) and its quizzes teach that distinction, since conflating them is how one good year becomes "an edge". **No lessons manifest exists** — the catalogue is globbed at runtime by `lessons_service.py`, and `curriculum_map.md` is a stale planning doc that already stopped at 292, so nothing needed registering. `PM_REVIEW.md` — track K, 5 must-fixes), then **every load-bearing prescription was independently re-simulated by a 7-agent verification fleet before being pinned** (scripts archived in `verification_fleet/`). Rendered **18/18 (100%)**; **8 of 8** prompts carrying a non-empty holdings block in the same prompt (up to `GME ×500`, 95.8% of portfolio) shipped it **false**. The sibling prose call site *does* pass it, where the PM-only gate makes it a no-op; the floor's own sector cap reads the same data directly and IS enforced. CR040's shipped-dark class, degrading into a positive false claim rather than silence — and `test_cr026_sector_allocation.py:464-508` plus `dump_assembled_prompts.py:218` both call the builder directly, which is why CR143's `assembled/` corpus renders the feature *working*. **Both reviews blamed the wrong file** (`_build_room_sector_context` raising, or missing marks): `SectorMapProvider.get` cannot raise and the same run's `$9,411.21` value over `$7,161.28` cash proves live holdings and marks. **(2) The parser reads `narration`; the profile teaches `Reasoning:` — and the miss is disclosed as a lie.** GRAB 19:19:37Z returned `{"action":"MODIFY","size_pct":2.0,"entry":3.67,"stop":3.45,"target":5.89,"rationale":"…three complete sentences…"}`. `_normalize_pm_action` absorbs MODIFY→APPROVE, size is present, so the reformatter never fires and `narration` is `""`. **Re-run against HEAD's parser on the verbatim reply**: APPROVE 2.0% @ 3.67/3.45/5.89, `reason` = `_PM_NO_RATIONALE` — *"it wrote no rationale for the call … Treat it as an unexplained decision"* — amber-marked on the Verdict Board and written to the Decision Journal, **and false**. This corrects DEF232's own diagnosis of this exact run (`84bb2cf9`): prose existed, the parser dropped it on a key name; DEF232's 23/965 (2.4%) sub-40-char reasons size the class, not the mechanism. **1/18 (5.6%, CI [0.1%, 27.3%])**. **(3) The REPLACES line reconciles the output block and leaves the decision sequence contradicting it.** `_PM_VERDICT_FORMAT:183-185` covers `portfolio_manager.md:36-45` only; five further lines (`portfolio_manager.md:27,32`; `overlay_generator.py:471,475,477`) still order REJECT / MODIFY-AND-APPROVE. The parser survives (`REJECT`→PASS, `MODIFY-*`→APPROVE); the user does not — **6/18 (33.3%, CI [13.3%, 59.0%])** narrations say *"rejected"* inside a **PASS**, one opening literally `"PASS — REJECTED due to mandate conflict"`, while `room_screen.dart:1158-1172` paints PASS **slate** and REJECT **amber** with a comment saying PASS must not read as a rejection (DEF056) — and amber REJECT is a real, different state meaning the floor overrode the PM. **The tag line is not unsatisfiable — both reviews were wrong.** *"End every verdict with this exact line"* lands **inside** `narration`: **1/18 epoch, 48/811 all-time**. Grep-verified there is no per-verdict disclaimer anywhere in `mobile/lib` (`disclaimerShort` is used once, on the share card), so a legal-framing sentence appears in the justification field ~6% of the time and nowhere the other 94% — CLAUDE.md's *"prompt instructions are not controls"*, stated backwards. **Four tiers.** **A (two lines, no prompt change):** pass `sector_weights` at `:3655` and make `_format_sector_allocation`'s empty state distinguish *no holdings* from *no weights supplied*; accept `rationale`/`reasoning` as `narration` aliases at `:955`. Both **defect-shaped — ask the Architect to mint two `DEF###`**; this CR is the evidence file. Guards ship in the same commit: a *production-path* parity test (not another direct `build_room_messages` call, which is what let this through) and a verbatim pin of the GRAB reply. **B (prompt diff, must be re-measured):** rewrite the decision sequence in the two-action vocabulary in both layers and widen the REPLACES sentence. Three checked constraints: `test_room_prompt_parity.py:68` asserts a MODIFY token survives (three lines supply it, so removing the `## Output format` block alone stays green; removing the vocabulary everywhere turns it red — the CR105 trap); the same block is the **only** format instruction on the PM's 1-on-1 surface (`agent_runner.py:160`, no `_PM_VERDICT_FORMAT`, nothing parses it) so it may be replaced but never deleted; and the floor itself is not editable except in the tag-line sentence — make the classroom disclosure structural instead. **C (one render block, data already on `ctx`):** current drawdown (`api/room.py:188` → hard-blocks at `safety_floor.py:546`), `existing_open_risk_pct` and the trade-pace counts are all computed for the floor and shown to nobody, while the prompt demands current drawdown **three times across two layers**. Ranked last on evidence: the PM **omits rather than fabricates** — `0/18` epoch narrations and `0/811` all-time reasons state a current-drawdown figure — so the reviewer's "Mid" impact is one notch high. De-duplicate against CR155 Tier C, same render. **D (docs only):** `safety_floor.md:81` and `agent_prompts.py:95` claim the floor is appended *last* for recency dominance; in the Room a median **15,794 chars** follow it (69% of a median 22,788-char prompt), 18/18. True on the 1-on-1 surface only; correct the docs, move nothing. **Claims REJECTED after checking:** *"upstream inputs missing"* (dead — median 10,121 chars of transcript in 18/18); *"an APPROVE cannot be filled from block numbers"* (dead — the reference position, debator sizes and the AMI-verified R:R supply it; 3 epoch APPROVEs, every level sourced `pm`); *"the portfolio breaches the cap it must enforce"* (**zero** over-cap holdings across all 18 prompts checked against each prompt's own cap; SNOA's 95.8% GME sits under a 100% cap); *"the tag line can never appear"* (false, above); *"render market cap"* (correct but **already CR145 Tier A** — PM-specific evidence handed over: 33/811 reasons invoke microcap/illiquidity language, 0/811 state a market cap); routing a floor flag into the verdict (out of scope by construction — the floor is the sole vetoer, DEF059); DEF236/DEF235/`LearningStyle.QUICK`/per-agent fact sheet (CR145 — and none binds here: the PM gets `_PM_VERDICT_FORMAT`, not `_PROSE_FORMAT`). **What is NOT broken, and it sets the priority:** first-pass parse **18/18 (100%)**, `_reformat_pm_response` **0/18** (the stub's 18.4% was a pooling artefact), CR105's 31.7% banned-action rate re-derives to **1/18 (5.6%)**, length guide **0/18** over budget against DEF236's 61–100% for the prose agents, format compliance 18/18, PM correctly excluded from the stance envelope. **Could not verify:** whether A2 accounts for all 23 of DEF232's sub-40-char reasons (raw replies not exported); whether `_build_room_sector_context` returns non-empty weights on Alpha (container restarted 08-08 08:37Z, epoch logs gone, no DB read available) — **so A1's acceptance must assert a real allocation renders, not merely that the kwarg is passed**; whether the 6% tag-line rate is stable. **Acceptance:** ≥30 convenes — real sector weights ≥95% and zero false empty-state lines; the GRAB reply parses to the model's own three sentences with DEF231's direction-signal rate re-measured *before* (recovering these narrations enlarges the checker's input population); REJECT-inside-PASS ≤10%; the disclosure present on 100% by construction or 0% with the instruction removed, never 6%; `test_room_prompt_parity.py` green with any change to its MODIFY assertion re-justified in the same commit; `pytest backend/tests/unit/ -q` green. **The headline:** the Portfolio Manager follows its instructions better than any other agent in the Room — every finding above is ours, not the model's. | proposed | [CR156_portfolio_manager_prompt_review/](CR156_portfolio_manager_prompt_review/) | AT:R66 |
| CR157 | 2026-08-08 | quality | **Weekly retrospective loop: score convened Rooms against reality, post-mortem the misses.** Saiful, 2026-08-08: *"This is the improvement loop CR. We will look back at the rooms that were convened and the results that were concluded. We need to check 'prediction' against reality, maybe weekly, on non-trading days, and do a post mortem on the quality of the ticker evaluation and prediction."* Out of CR143: the 12-agent audit (external_review/room/kimi/) measured *process* quality (grounding, format, scope) but nothing measures *outcome* quality — whether a Room's conclusion about a ticker was actually right. This CR closes that loop. **What it builds.** **(1) Scoreable-conclusion capture.** Today `room_runs` persists ticker, timestamps, full transcript (JsonB) and verdict (JsonB) per run (`backend/app/db/models.py:530-557`) — the raw material already exists. What is NOT captured: the reference price at convene time, the Trader's entry/stop/target levels, and per-agent `[STANCE]` headers as structured fields (they live only inside transcript prose). Add a `room_run_conclusions` table (or JsonB column) populated at run end: reference price, PM verdict action + size, trader levels, per-agent stance/conviction/headline. **(2) Weekly scoring batch, non-trading days.** A job (systemd timer on melehost, precedent in `infra/systemd/`; weekend UTC so US market closes are final) pulls realized prices via the existing yfinance history path (`market_data.py` CachingProvider — no new provider) and scores every conclusion aged ≥7 days: direction correctness vs reference price, target-hit / stop-hit where levels exist, vs a same-window buy-and-hold baseline. Multiple horizons (1w, 4w) so fast feedback doesn't force short-termism into a long-horizon product. **(3) Post-mortem report.** Per-agent scorecard — which agents' stances correlated with outcomes, split by conviction — plus failure classification using the CR143 taxonomy (E1 hallucination / E2 arithmetic / E3 format / E4 scope / E5 missing-state) so a bad outcome is traced to a cause class, not just counted. Output lands in `docs/forward_planning/CR143_agent_prompt_audit/` (or a successor home) as the standing evidence base for future prompt CRs, and feeds the eval-harness golden set. **Discipline constraints.** Scores are an internal quality signal, never user-facing — a lucky PM PASS is not "advice that worked". Never pool rates across mandate regimes (the CR153/CR156 lesson: three different single-name caps in one epoch corpus already burned one audit). Small-n honesty: per-agent sample sizes will be single-digit for weeks; report confidence, not verdicts. Rooms the user never acted on still score — the conclusion is the unit of quality, not the trade. **Out of scope:** changing any agent behaviour, auto-tuning prompts from scores (a later CR, gated on this one producing trustworthy data), any brokerage/live-trading linkage. **Acceptance:** conclusions captured on 100% of new runs; the weekly batch runs unattended on a non-trading day and scores all due conclusions; the post-mortem names at least the cause class of every scored miss; one full cycle demonstrated on real Alpha data before any prompt change cites it. | proposed | [CR157_weekly_retrospective_loop/](CR157_weekly_retrospective_loop/) | AT:R66 |
| CR158 | 2026-08-08 | infra | **Stamp a prompt version, so a measurement can tell which prompt produced it.** Saiful, 2026-08-08: *"when will we update the frontmatter?"* — asked after DEF241/DEF243 changed prompt bytes in three `content/agents/*.md` files. The direct answer is that nothing needed updating: the frontmatter is four identity keys (`agent_id`, `display_name`, `family`, `role_color`), identical across all 13 files, carrying no version — and **nothing in the backend parses it at all**. The question exposes the real gap. **There is no prompt version anywhere in the system.** `llm_audit` has 19 columns and stores `system_prompt` verbatim, but nothing records which prompt generation produced a row; `room_runs` has no such field either. **The cost is already paid, twice.** CR143's entire method rests on epoch-partitioning, and every boundary had to be reconstructed **by hand from git SHAs** (`7fc09420` CR105, `258625a7` DEF227-229, `06098b4f` DEF233/231/232, `3f4d33d2` DEF234) — a manual step with no check on it. It produced a wrong published figure: the 18.4% PM-reformatter rate filed in CR143 pooled a 30-day window across a prompt change; on the current epoch it is 0/18, and the same error made stance emission read 4.5% when 1,682 of the pooled turns predated the envelope shipping. It also cost four independent subagents time apiece: `real_samples/*.prompt.txt` for the market, news, research-manager and trader agents are all pre-DEF228 captures that render a fact-sheet shape HEAD can no longer emit, and each subagent had to discover that for itself because nothing in the file says which generation it is. **It matters now, not in the abstract:** DEF241 and DEF243 both owe a post-promotion re-measure, and today the only way to separate pre- from post-promotion turns is timestamp-versus-deploy-time, reconstructed by hand — the exact step that already produced one wrong number in this programme. **Scope.** (1) A `prompt_version` in each agent file's frontmatter — content-derived, not hand-maintained, or it drifts the way `INDEX.md` did: a short hash over the six assembly layers (`GROUNDING_DIRECTIVE`, base `.md`, mandate overlay, user overlay, format constants, safety floor) computed at import, so it changes exactly when the assembled prompt changes and cannot be forgotten in a commit. (2) One nullable `prompt_version` column on `llm_audit`, written by the gateway alongside `system_prompt`. Nullable and additive — old rows stay NULL, which honestly means "unversioned", not "version zero" (CR040). (3) A guard asserting every agent file carries the key, so a new agent cannot ship unstamped. **Explicitly NOT in scope:** hand-written semantic versions (they drift silently and a drifted version is worse than none), backfilling historical rows (the SHA reconstruction in `CR143_agent_prompt_audit/README.md` stays the record for pre-CR158 epochs), and any change to what the prompts say. **Acceptance:** two convenes either side of a deliberate prompt edit carry different `prompt_version` values; a convene with no prompt change carries the same one; `test_config_compose_parity.py` stays green (the column needs no env, but the migration does need the DEF215 ownership rule — Alembic owns the table, `init_schema` must not `create_all` it). **BUILT 2026-08-09, before the promotion** — so the DEF240/241/243 re-measure is the first thing it makes exact. `app/services/prompt_version.py` hashes the **fully assembled prompt across a fixed MATRIX of reference mandates** (grounding directive + base file + mandate overlay + format constants + mandate snapshot + Room block + safety floor), not the base file: **ROUND-1 AUDIT MAJOR — it shipped as a single reference at `risk_score: 3`, and the auditor broke it on the first attempt using the branch this submission had itself named as the risk.** They edited text inside `_aggressive_block`'s `if m.risk_score <= 2:` branch — real copy a low-risk user's Aggressive Debator receives — and the version did not move (`86c3b410b5c0` before and after). A prompt change would have shipped while the column reported "nothing changed" **for exactly the population it changed for**: CR143's silent mis-partitioning reproduced across a mandate-shape boundary instead of a time boundary, i.e. the column lying precisely where it is trusted. Fixed with a 3-mandate matrix spanning every axis the assembly branches on — `risk_score` (≤2/3/≥4), `halal`, `long_only`, `ticker_blocklist`, `path`, `horizon` — hashed together, built by `model_copy` because `hydrate_coach_mandate` silently ignores the compliance axes from a spec dict and would have produced three identical mandates that *looked* fixed. **Completeness is proven, not argued:** `test_the_matrix_executes_every_line_of_every_role_block` traces the assembly with `sys.settrace` and fails if any executable line of any role-block function goes unexecuted. **It immediately found a sixth axis I had not enumerated** — `_fundamentals_block` branches on `m.horizon`, and all three mandates were LONG or VERY_LONG — which is the whole argument for the guard over a careful reading. all 12 Room agents resolve, all 12 distinct, deterministic across calls, and **no database is touched** (`user_id=None` means no user overlay and no journal block — asserted by a test that fails if a session is ever opened). Computed lazily and cached per agent. The Concierge is an explicit quiet `None` rather than an exception — it has no Room phase, and routing it through the failure path would log a warning on every Concierge call, spending a degrade-loudly signal on an expected case. Column: `llm_audit.prompt_version`, nullable, no server_default, no backfill (migration `b7c31f9d4e05`, CR141's shape, DEF215's ownership rule). **NULL means unversioned, never version zero** — the same CR040 distinction the `*_tokens` columns draw, and it is also what a failed assembly or an agentless flow records. **Mutation proof, 9 of 9 killed:** hashing the base file only (the exact failure the CR was written against — kills 11); dropping the grounding directive; returning a sentinel string instead of `None` on failure; the gateway not stamping; `record_llm_call` dropping the kwarg; a non-constant reference input; **collapsing the matrix back to one mandate (the round-1 MAJOR, exactly — kills 6)**; dropping the horizon axis the coverage guard found; and hashing only the first mandate's assembly. **Two survived the first pass and both are recorded rather than quietly patched:** nothing covered the failure path (a sentinel would be counted as a real generation by any `GROUP BY prompt_version`, silently merging every failed run into one fake epoch), and — **the DEF238 blind spot for the third time in this programme** — nothing asserted the gateway actually wires the version into the audit row; every test proved `prompt_version()` and `record_llm_call()` in isolation, so deleting the stamp at the call site left all 15 green. Both now have end-to-end tests driving the real `LLMGateway.stream_chat`. Six behavioural tests assert the version MOVES for a change to `_PROSE_FORMAT`, `_STANCE_FORMAT`, the grounding directive, a role overlay, and `_LENGTH_GUIDE` — none of which live in any agent `.md` file, which is the whole argument for not hashing one — and one asserts it does NOT move for a user's own mandate, since a per-user version would partition users instead of prompt generations. Related: CR143 (the audit that paid this cost), DEF241/DEF243 (whose acceptance needs it), DEF215 (schema ownership), CR141 (the last `llm_audit` column addition — same migration shape, `2a08e21c0dac`). | done | [CR158_prompt_version_stamp/](CR158_prompt_version_stamp/) | AT:R66 |
| CR159 | 2026-08-09 | quality | **"Your Firm" — give the Floor's flat hex grid a desk structure (View A). May or may not be built.** Saiful, 2026-08-09: *"The new screen design will be a different CR. It may or may not be built."* Filed as a design of record so the thinking survives even if the build never happens. Out of the same competitive review as CR160: since the agent graph is inherited and not defensible, differentiation has to live in **persistence and accountability** — the things a repo structurally cannot have and a product can. This is step one. **It is not a new screen.** [`mobile/lib/screens/floor/floor_screen.dart`](../../../mobile/lib/screens/floor/floor_screen.dart) (541 lines, tab 0) already renders all 12 agents as tappable hexes in a centred `Wrap` at line 409, with lock states, the earn-path sheet and a coach-mark tour. CR159 replaces that flat `Wrap` with desk-banded tiers; everything else on the Floor stays. **The display.** Hierarchy comes from **vertical order and band labels, not drawn lines** — a real org chart is wide, a phone is narrow, and any tree with 13 nodes forces horizontal scroll or pinch-zoom. Tiers read top-to-bottom the way people already read on mobile and no band ever scrolls sideways: `YOU` → `CIO` → `ANALYST DESK 4/4` → `RESEARCH 2/3` → `EXECUTION 1/1` + `RISK 0/3` sharing a band (Execution is one agent; a full-width band wastes a third of the fold) → `CONCIERGE — reports to you`. Three choices carry the weight. **(1) Locked renders as an unfilled seat, not a locked feature** — same earn-path data, reframed as hiring, so a firm with three empty risk seats reads as *your firm, incomplete*; that is the CEO metaphor doing work instead of being asserted in a tagline. **(2) The band header reserves a slot for standing** — `4/4` today, hit-rate or override-rate when the accountability CR lands, which makes that CR purely additive. **(3) Selection highlight is deliberately left unused** — it is the hook View B (the pipeline) needs, tracing handoffs across the same hexes; `kAgentPhase` in `mobile/lib/models/agent.dart` already holds that data client-side. Tap behaviour is unchanged: the existing `agent_action_sheet` still opens. **Four traps found by reading the code, not by design review.** **T-TOUR:** `FloorTour` anchors `GlobalKey`s `_agentKey0`/`_agentKey4` to *positions* in the flat `Wrap` ([`floor_screen.dart:47-52`](../../../mobile/lib/screens/floor/floor_screen.dart#L47-L52)); re-banding moves both, so they must be re-anchored to named agents and the tour re-run on a real device. **T-SLICE:** lines 342-343 do `concierge = kAllAgents.last` and `tradingAgents = kAllAgents.sublist(0, 12)` — grouping must derive from a field, never list position, or the next roster edit silently mis-assigns a desk. **T-TWICE:** `HexAvatar` renders in **10 files**, and CR106 already fought exactly this — two renderers of one dataset, neither a superset, which produced DEF143. The Floor and the Verdict Board's consensus comb (`kCombVoices`) would drift; mitigation is one shared band widget plus a parity test shaped like `test_cr106_board_parity`. **T-SEQUENCE:** CR160 must land first — both CRs edit `agent.dart`, and doing this one first means redoing every band label. **Data change:** add an `AgentDesk` enum + `desk` field to `agent.dart`, mirrored in `backend/app/schemas/agents.py` — `officeOfCio` / `analyst` / `research` / `execution` / `risk` / `concierge`. **Do not overload `AgentFamily`**: it lumps Research Manager with the PM as `manager`, which is wrong hierarchically (Research Manager sits *inside* Research, the CIO sits *above everything*). A sweep shows `AgentFamily` is read in only three places, all `== AgentFamily.concierge` checks, so changing it would be safe — but there is no reason to make one field mean two things. **Out of scope:** per-agent standing/track record (separate CR; this one only reserves the slot), View B, any change to `agent_id`, and the rename itself. **Acceptance:** `flutter test` green including new desk-coverage and Floor↔comb parity tests; release build to iPhone — the tour and the unfilled-seat state both need a real device, not a simulator screenshot; at 390pt portrait no band scrolls horizontally and the YOU/CIO topper plus at least two bands sit above the fold. | proposed | [CR159_your_firm_desk_structure/](CR159_your_firm_desk_structure/) | AT:R66 |
| CR160 | 2026-08-09 | quality | **Rename six agent roles away from the TradingAgents lineage.** Saiful, 2026-08-08: *"Change the debators, portfolio managers, traders, market analysts, soc meds, and news analysts. Keep bull and bears, they are market jargons. But yes, we will use your suggestions for the AR/MS."* Out of the competitive review in [`docs/external/anthropic_financial_services_comparison.md`](../../external/anthropic_financial_services_comparison.md) §7: our agent graph *is* TradingAgents' figure 1, and that project is Apache-2.0 at ★96,365 (measured 2026-08-08), so the architecture is not defensible IP. Everything we added on top — mandate overlay, Brief Your Agent, the deterministic safety floor, the Decision Journal — is invisible when it works, so the surface answer to "what is this?" is still theirs. **Recorded honestly: renaming buys surface distinctiveness, not architectural differentiation** — the lineage stays recognisable to anyone comparing graphs. It earns its place on three independent grounds instead. **(1) A spelling bug in shipped copy.** "Debator" is not an English word; it appears in user-visible strings across 272 files. The rename deletes the word, so **no separate DEF is needed — this CR subsumes it**. **(2) Two names misdescribe a simulation-only product.** "Trader" names an agent that never executes a trade; "Portfolio Manager" implies managing real money. **(3) Translation gets more expensive at v1.0, not cheaper.** **The renames:** Aggressive/Conservative/Neutral Debator → **Risk Officer — Aggressive / Conservative / Balanced** (`AGG`/`CON`/`BAL`); Portfolio Manager → **Chief Investment Officer** (`CIO` — the user is CEO, so CIO is the natural direct report); Trader → **Execution Desk** (`EXEC`); Market Analyst → **Technical Strategist** (`TECH`); Social Media Analyst → **Flow & Positioning** (`FLOW` — "social media" ages badly); News Analyst → **Macro & Events** (`MACRO`). **Unchanged:** Fundamentals Analyst, Bull Researcher, Bear Researcher, Research Manager, AMI Concierge — bull/bear are genuine market jargon, not TradingAgents coinage. `role_color` and `AgentFamily` untouched. **AR/MS is transcreation, not translation, and it is the highest-risk detail here.** Bull/Bear survive in EN but not in Arabic or Malay, where a literal rendering yields an animal rather than a market stance; the localised strings use **Long-Side / Short-Side** instead. That is a deliberate divergence from the EN source, so the i18n files must carry a context comment saying so — otherwise the first translator to read it "corrects" it back to ثور/دب. **Scope.** In: [`mobile/lib/models/agent.dart`](../../../mobile/lib/models/agent.dart) (the entire client surface is this one registry — `displayName` + `abbreviation`), its backend mirror `backend/app/schemas/agents.py`, `content/agents/*.md` frontmatter plus in-prompt cross-references ("That's the Trader's job"), `content/` at large (**3,348 occurrences** measured 2026-08-08 across lessons, daily challenges, glossary, ai_coach), `website/` + `website_api/` (21 occurrences), and the i18n strings. **Out: `agent_id` is not touched** — it is a DB key with unique constraints across five tables (`user_overlays`, overlay counts, activations and two more, [`backend/app/db/models.py:286-410`](../../../backend/app/db/models.py#L286-L410)) and Brief Your Agent history is keyed on it, so a migration buys nothing a user can see. `aggressive_debator` remains an identifier forever; only its label moves. Prompt file names stay for the same reason. No behaviour change. **Sequencing: land before CR159**, which edits the same registry to add a grouping field. **Open decision:** *Flow & Positioning* is the correct desk term but a beginner will not parse it, and this is a teaching product — *Sentiment & Flow* keeps a familiar word. Defaulting to the former per instruction; must be settled **before** the content sweep, since changing it after means re-running 3,348 substitutions and re-flagging translation. **Translation impact:** `content/daily_challenges/ms/` already exists, so this triggers MS re-translation per the standing content rule; AR has not started. Every touched id carries `retranslate:[ar,ms]`. **Acceptance:** zero occurrences of the six old labels as agent names across `mobile/lib`, `content/`, `website/`, `website_api/`; `agent_id` values byte-identical before and after, proven by an ID-column diff; existing Brief Your Agent overlays still resolve against **real rows, not a fixture**; i18n carries the Bull/Bear transcreation note; `pytest backend/tests/unit/ -q` and `flutter test` green; release build to device shows the Floor, the Verdict Board comb and one Room run rendering new labels with no truncation at 390pt. | proposed | [CR160_agent_rename/](CR160_agent_rename/) | AT:R66 |
| CR161 | 2026-08-09 | **White-label AMI Trade to brokerage houses (B2B2C programme).** Saiful, 2026-08-09: *"mean to use the skill to plan our GTM activity as a white label app, offering to other brokerage houses."* **Why it is coherent and not a reversal:** our own competitive analysis named the trap first — *"the obvious business model for a consumer trading app is to become a brokerage, and we have locked ourselves out of that by decision. That is simultaneously our moat and our monetisation constraint"* (`docs/external/anthropic_financial_services_comparison.md`). White-label is the exit that keeps the moat: we do not become a broker, we sell to brokers, and that doc's quadrant 3 (broker-attached consumer AI — Robinhood Cortex, Webull Vega, Moomoo) is precisely the capability every *other* retail broker feels behind on and cannot build. Locked as **[D-069](../../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md)**, a *partial* amendment of D-004: a brokerage may be a **customer**; **no order routing, no execution venue, no order-flow integration, ever** — for a tenant exactly as for our own users. Every prospect asks; the answer is pre-decided and not negotiable per deal. `vision_and_positioning.md`'s "B2B / institutional sales — out of scope" line rewritten to match. **Measured readiness (live melehost + repo, 2026-08-08/09), not estimated.** The alpha *is* the reference deployment a broker will ask about: 168 user rows (32 new in 7d, 71 in 14d), 58 have ever convened the Room, **12 WAU** (31 runs; 24/14d, 44/30d), 1,018 total Room runs, **30% activation** (21 of 71 new-14d users ran a Room), **8% claimed accounts (13/168)**, devices active-14d **Android 42 · iOS 9**, and ~28 distinct builds in the wild spanning `0.1.0+43`…`+70`. Two readings: 30% activation and 1,018 real runs is a non-trivial evidence base; **12 weekly actives is too thin to be a case study**, and at 8% claimed we cannot segment who those 12 are. **Gaps that gate a sale:** multi-tenancy **does not exist** (no tenant model, no brand config, no theme config anywhere in `backend/app` or `mobile/lib`); "AMI" is hardcoded in **51** `app_en.arb` entries, across backend agent files, and **98** lesson files, and CLAUDE.md's own naming rule (*"app copy → AMI by name"*) is actively hostile to white-label and needs a carve-out; **DEF178 open** (live `sk_live_…` key in git history, pushed to GitHub — any vendor security questionnaire finds it) and **DEF182 open** (`SECRET_KEY` reused as the Alpaca encryption key, crypto fails open — blocks the rotation that is DEF178's own remediation, so 182 is first); product analytics is a **phantom** (see DEF246); commercial terms do not exist (pricing is B2C only — no SLA, DPA, data-residency position or security-questionnaire pack). **Four workstreams:** (1) prospecting via `vibe-prospecting` — third-party Explorium, **not** an Anthropic skill despite the marketplace framing, needs a Saiful-provisioned account; ICP tiered by where the differentiators land — Tier 1 GCC/Malaysia/Indonesia retail brokers (halal + AR/MS absent from every incumbent: StockTrak, Etna Soft, InvestSuite, Devexperts/Huddlestock), Tier 2 mid-size Western brokers with no AI layer, Tier 3 Islamic banks/takaful/universities/exchange education arms; Saiful owns all outreach, Claude never sends. (2) Turn the alpha into evidence — wire PostHog for real, attack the 8% claim rate, close DEF182→DEF178. (3) Make it white-labelable (own CR: tenant model, brand tokens, and the re-skin-vs-re-design call that decides weeks vs months) — **do not sell ahead of this; a signed broker with no tenancy layer is worse than no broker**. (4) Commercial + legal (Saiful + lawyer, only once a Tier-1 prospect responds). **Honest positioning note for the pitch pack:** the Room's *architecture* is not defensible IP (TradingAgents Apache-2.0 ★96k, ai-hedge-fund MIT ★63k — rebuildable in a weekend); the moat is deterministic mandate/safety-floor enforcement, the sourced CR060 corpus, halal + AR/MS, and shipping a real mobile product. Sell that, not the agent count.
