| CR162 | 2026-08-10 | **Two-platform automated UI testing — extend the CR080 harness to iPhone.** Saiful, 2026-08-10: *"do a research for me on how to do automated testing on android and iphone."* Research found Android already solved (CR080's `qa/appium/`: Appium + UiAutomator2, 11 test modules, black-box against the release APK on the Galaxy A17) and **iOS at literally zero** — `mobile/ios/RunnerTests/RunnerTests.swift` is the untouched Flutter template stub and every iOS check has always been Saiful driving a phone by hand. **The gap is a Flutter engine limitation, not neglect.** Flutter paints to a canvas with no native widgets, so every black-box tool reads the accessibility **semantics tree**. Android builds that tree the moment an accessibility client interrogates the window — which is precisely why CR080 needed no app change. iOS gates it on `UIAccessibilityIsVoiceOverRunning() || UIAccessibilityIsSwitchControlRunning()`, so on a real iPhone XCUITest sees the whole app as **one opaque `FlutterView`** with empty page source ([flutter#25485](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/25485), filed Dec 2018, **still open**). Signing and tooling are not the blocker. **The unlock:** `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()` forces semantics collection regardless of assistive tech — ~10 lines behind `--dart-define=AMI_QA_SEMANTICS=1`, inert in shipping builds. **The second half:** `SemanticsProperties.identifier` (Flutter ≥3.19; we are on 3.41.9) maps to `resource-id` on Android and `accessibilityIdentifier` on iOS, ships in release, invisible to users — *one* locator strategy for both platforms, which is what lets this extend the existing harness instead of forking a second one. It also fixes a live Android problem: the app has **no stable test IDs at all** (0 `Key('` in `mobile/lib`, 0 `identifier:`, 9 files using `Semantics(`), so `helpers/locators.py` finds everything by rendered text and `config/locales.py` must carry every EN/AR/MS string verbatim just to tap a bottom-nav tab — navigation is coupled to translation, and every ARB edit is a potential harness break. **Explicitly supersedes CR080's `## Not changed` promise that "nothing in `mobile/lib/` changes"** — correct for Android, unachievable for iOS; recorded here so the edits are not later read as undocumented drift. Delivers: Phase 0 app-side gate + narrow `Semantics(identifier:)` on `hex_bottom_nav.dart`/`hex_button.dart`/the modal sheets + a widget test that fails if the IDs are dropped; Phase 1 platform abstraction across `config/devices.py` (note the bundle-id mismatch — iOS `ai.agenticmarketintel.amiTrade` vs Android `ai.agenticmarketintel.ami_trade`), `config/capabilities.py` (`XCUITestOptions`, `waitForQuiescence=False` as the analogue of Android's `waitForIdleTimeout=100` for the always-animating `TickerTape`), `helpers/locators.py` (`by_id()` on `ACCESSIBILITY_ID`), `helpers/device.py` (`xcrun simctl` path; iOS has no nav bar so the DEF075-class check becomes bottom-safe-area/home-indicator intrusion), `conftest.py` (`--platform`/`AMI_PLATFORM`); Phase 2 iOS Simulator bring-up (Appium 3 + XCUITest ≥10; Node 25 + Xcode 26.6 already present, Appium not installed) porting `test_00_smoke_hierarchy.py` first as the GO/NO-GO gate; Phase 3 closes two standing gaps — a `ubuntu-latest` CI job running `flutter analyze lib/` + `flutter test` (**70 files / ~525 mobile cases currently run only when a human remembers**; `deploy-beta.yml` is the only workflow, `workflow_dispatch`-only, backend pytest alone) at $0.006/min versus $0.062/min and a 10× multiplier on macOS runners, and the melehost drift guard CR080 flagged as a second occurrence with *"no guard designed yet"* after a hand-edited remote copy produced a bogus 27-FAIL report from one `TypeError`. **Rejected:** Patrol (strongest Flutter-native tool in 2026, but needs *instrumented* builds — discards CR080's deliberate "test the real release artifact" property and means a Dart rewrite of the Python harness; re-openable); Maestro (does not natively support real iOS devices at all — simulator or a cloud vendor only, same semantics problem with less control); cloud device farms (BrowserStack ~$129/mo/parallel, Sauce RDC from $199/mo, Firebase Test Lab $5/device-hr and weak on iOS — buys device-matrix *breadth*, not the missing thing, and uploads a stealth-alpha build to a third party; revisit at beta). **Out of scope, stated not dropped:** real iPhone 17 via WebDriverAgent (needs WDA signed against Saiful's Apple dev account + Developer Mode; next step once the simulator suite is green, and a device profile + signing caps rather than new code), iOS golden/screenshot regression, and the Appium Phase 2 flows still blocked on credentials. **Acceptance turns on one question:** with `AMI_QA_SEMANTICS=1` does an XCUITest page source contain the bottom-nav identifiers as addressable elements, and with the flag off does it collapse to one `FlutterView` — if the first fails, stop and report rather than papering over it with coordinate taps. | CR163 | 2026-08-10 | **An autonomous bug crawler on the simulator — find defects nobody thought to write a test for, and feed them to the fixer/auditor pipeline.** Saiful, 2026-08-10: *"since we are running lean, I want to be able to use the simulations to work out bugs so they can be fixed. I need you to create a framework where we can do this autonomously."* The existing harness (CR080, CR162) only finds bugs someone already imagined — every check is an assertion a human wrote about a screen a human listed — which does not scale for a one-person team and structurally cannot find the surprising defects, which are the expensive ones. **CR162 made the alternative possible:** once the accessibility semantics tree is exposed the app is *enumerable*, so the harness can list every addressable control and explore on its own; coverage then grows by walking further rather than by writing more tests. Three separated parts: **explorer** (`crawler/explorer.py`, breadth-first walk under a wall-clock budget), **oracles** (`crawler/oracles.py` + `crawler/errorsink.py` — anything that can call a screen wrong with no screen-specific assertion: Flutter framework errors, layout overflow, controls under the safe area, sparse screens, unlabelled controls), and **ledger + triage** (`crawler/ledger.py`, `tools/triage.py` — fingerprint, suppress what is already triaged, promote the rest). Entry point `scripts/crawl_ios_sim.sh`. **The finding that redirected the design, measured rather than assumed:** the first implementation read Flutter's errors from the device log, and that does not work — a `simctl spawn log stream` capture of a live `Runner` process, taken while the app was actively calling `debugPrint`, returned **5,685 lines and zero Dart-origin entries**; every apparent "flutter" match was a CFBundle resource lookup. Dart stdout/stderr goes to the process's own stdout, which `os_log` never sees (`flutter run` shows those lines only because it holds the pipe). So the app records its own errors instead — `mobile/lib/qa/error_sink.dart` installs `FlutterError.onError` + `PlatformDispatcher.onError` behind CR162's existing `--dart-define=AMI_QA_SEMANTICS=1` and appends de-duplicated JSONL to the app container, which the crawler reads back via `simctl get_app_container`; uniform across platforms, survives the crawler crashing, no new transport. **Debug build by Saiful's call** — Flutter compiles most framework assertions out of release, so a release crawl finds only hard crashes; the trade is that timing-sensitive findings are leads, not measurements. **The crawler deliberately files nothing.** CR080 twice had a harness bug written up as application failures, the worst being one `TypeError` reported as 27 failing tests, none real — and Saiful's pipeline puts a **fixer agent waiting on whatever is filed**, so an auto-filing crawler plus an auto-fixing agent turns one bad build into a branch full of fixes for defects that never existed. `tools/triage.py` is the gate; it writes **intake stubs**, not `DEF###` rows, because ids are minted by a single owner to avoid collisions and a script minting them autonomously is exactly that race. From the stub the existing machinery takes over: Architect mints + writes the assign lane → `coder.*` fixes → auditor verdict (`DISPATCH_PROTOCOL.md`). **Decisions not to re-litigate:** the frontier holds *replayable paths*, not screen fingerprints (the first version queued fingerprints, which is unimplementable — there is no `goto(fingerprint)` — so depth > 1 silently never worked); the budget is wall-clock, not step count (steps range 200ms–seconds, so a step budget makes runs incomparable); destructive controls are never tapped, and the deny-list is asserted in `tests_offline/` rather than trusted, because this drives the real Alpha backend with a real account; the scroll oracle runs LAST because it swipes, and the explorer re-reads controls afterwards rather than tapping nodes enumerated before the screen moved; a missing error sink is a hard failure and never "no errors found"; and seen ≠ triaged, so a merely-reported finding keeps being reported until an explicit `filed`/`false_positive`/`wontfix` decision silences it. **Out of scope:** scheduling (Saiful chose "on-demand now, scheduled once it's proven"), Android (the design is platform-neutral — the sink is a file on both — but only the iOS simulator path is built here), and auto-fixing (the fixer + auditor already exist in `orchestration/dispatch/`; this feeds them). | CR164 | 2026-08-10 | quality | **Room backtesting harness — as-of mode on the production infrastructure, EDGAR point-in-time fundamentals, staged pilot→full sweep.** Saiful, 2026-08-10: plan a backtest of the Room; free to collect + store data for reuse; survivor-bias- and news-availability-aware; "limited backtest" acceptable if justified. Binding design rule from plan review: **same infrastructure as the main app** — no forked data layer or Room path, so any infra change is re-testable by re-running the harness. Locked decisions: outcome edge primary (1w/4w forward returns, APPROVE vs PASS vs random-pick vs SPY); staged ~130-convene pilot → ~800–1000 full; news ablated in v1 (schema reserves `news_archive` for an Alpha-Vantage/GDELT arm); social ablated (no historical endpoint; CR035 arm-C precedent); **EDGAR companyfacts PIT fundamentals in v1** (filed-date-keyed, leakage-correct). What it builds: (1) `AsOfContext` threaded per-run via ContextVar — request-scoped, never env-flipped (reversal of CR035's arm mechanism that degraded live Alpha); (2) `price_history_daily` extended to OHLCV with `as_of` cutoff reads — one price store for Room, Portfolio Health, and scoring; (3) `fetch_fundamentals(ticker, as_of=None)` — one module, live yfinance path vs EDGAR PIT path, identical dict shape; non-reconstructable fields (forward P/E, PEG, analyst target/rating, next earnings) flow to the existing `field_state = UNAVAILABLE` machinery (CR104/DEF123), structurally not prompt-instructed; (4) admin-only `POST /v1/admin/backtest/room-run` (public `RoomStartRequest` never grows the field); (5) sweep driver factored from `room_benchmark.py`, resumable, run inside the alpha container; (6) scoring from the snapshot store only (byte-reproducible), date-clustered inference (effective n ≈ #as-of dates), per-date random-pick bootstrap null, target/stop-hit gated on `level_provenance`; (7) structural leakage guards: store-level `AsOfLeakageError`, post-run `llm_audit` prompt scan, model-cutoff probe fixing `window_start = collapse-month + 8w` (both benchmark lanes — `docs/benchmark/claude/`, `kimi/` — hold pre-cutoff LLM backtests invalid on their face; only ~late-2025→mid-2026 is scoreable). Survivorship: `tickers_150` reused with a written membership audit (`backtest_universe_membership`), counts published verbatim. Payoff beyond the one-off result: a pinned regression batch (same spec, new batch_id) makes "infra changed → re-test the Room" a routine ~1.5 h operation. Limitations register ships with the report (no Sharpe — no SELL/portfolio; ~12% verdict-flip noise floor; tested Room ≠ live Room under ablations). Related: CR035 (the harness lineage), CR136 (`price_history_daily`), CR157 (weekly retrospective of live runs — distinct, stays proposed), CR158 (`prompt_version` epochs). | CR165 | 2026-08-11 | **A dispassionate catalogue of the 50 largest US/English YouTube channels that claim to teach investing — URL, strategy class, monetisation, and what each sells.** Saiful, 2026-08-11: *"research the popolar internet and youtube channels that are now suggesting that they can teach you investing… this research is dispasionate. do not editorialized. that would be my job later on."* Scope answered by him: **US/English only**, YouTube as entry point **plus** the paid product it funnels to, **50 entries ranked by popularity**, tiered **15 full-detail / 15 four-to-eight lines / 20 two-to-three lines**. **The constraint that shaped the work is the no-editorializing one**, because a survey of this field invites judgement at every line: every entry is evidenced from the channel's **own About text and a sample of its most recent upload titles** (read from each channel's own YouTube page with `hl=en&gl=US`, 2026-08-11 — no count taken from a listicle); creator claims are quoted and attributed, never asserted and never rebutted in line; the **only ordering is subscriber count**, with no quality ranking anywhere; evaluative vocabulary is absent by construction and grep-verified; and **regulatory facts appear only with a primary source** (FTC/SEC/court by URL) — exactly one entry qualified, Warrior Trading's April 2022 FTC action ($3M, and $2.9M returned to 20,402 people in Jan 2023) — with absence documented as "nothing located", never as a clean record. Method: ~95 candidates from two independent seeds (published roundups, which over-index on passive/personal-finance creators, **and** YouTube channel-search per strategy term, the only way the trading-education half of the field surfaces at all), verified, screened by a stated inclusion rule, ranked, tiered. **Findings worth flagging, as facts:** popularity rank and strategy coverage pull in opposite directions — the 510K cut line removes almost the entire options, value, dividend and retirement-decumulation segments (tastylive, projectoption, Motley Fool, Timothy Sykes, Everything Money, Option Alpha, IBD and ~35 more sit below rank 50), so **Appendix A** lists them by strategy class rather than hiding the effect; two of the top 50 monetise the audience with **nothing** (Aswath Damodaran, Two Cents/PBS); two funnel to a **security** rather than education (Cardone Capital's funds, the Meet Kevin Pricing Power ETF); three large personal-finance-branded channels publish **no investing instruction in recent output** (Caleb Hammer, Erika Kullberg, Charlie Chang) and are kept at rank with an `adjacent` label and the evidence quoted rather than silently dropped; and vendor pricing is often unobtainable (warriortrading.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch), recorded as unverified rather than estimated. **Nothing was dropped silently** — **Appendix B** lists every screened-out channel with the rule that removed it (Valuetainment/Codie Sanchez = business, Karlton Dennis/Mark Kohler = tax, NickRTFM = EA FC Ultimate Team not securities, plus the non-US set: Coin Bureau, Rayner Teo, Ben Felix, Patrick Boyle et al). **Out of scope:** AR/MS creators (offered and declined for this pass), non-YouTube-first surfaces, audience-overlap or revenue estimation, and any assessment of teaching quality — Saiful does that pass.
